articles.title: El exdirector de Nvidia, Jensen Huang, aceptó declarar a puertas cerradas ante tres comisiones del Congreso
articles.text:
Jensen Huang, quien renunció el 12 de noviembre como director ejecutivo de Nvidia, aceptó declarar a puertas cerradas ante tres comisiones de la Cámara de Representantes de Estados Unidos sobre su relación con Alice Huang, una empresaria china señalada como presunta espía. Lo informó el congresista John Moolenaar.
Moolenaar, republicano por Michigan y presidente del comité de la Cámara que investiga al Partido Comunista Chino, lo dijo el domingo 15 de noviembre en el programa Face the Nation, de CBS. Aclaró que también irán representantes de Nvidia y que las fechas exactas todavía se negocian.
Las tres comisiones son la de Asuntos Exteriores, la de Inteligencia y el comité sobre China que preside Moolenaar. Según el congresista, Huang y Nvidia le dijeron que colaborarán con ellas. Al ser una comparecencia voluntaria, no hará falta emitir una citación judicial (subpoena, en inglés), confirmó a la conductora Margaret Brennan.
Los legisladores habían invitado a Huang el jueves 12 de noviembre a una entrevista a puertas cerradas, con transcripción, el 1 de diciembre, y advirtieron que si no cooperaba lo citarían por la fuerza. Moolenaar dijo que ahora se evalúan las fechas exactas.
Qué quieren saber los legisladores
Moolenaar explicó que la reunión busca “entender hasta qué punto se accedió a información privilegiada” y en qué medida la supuesta espía influyó en la filosofía de Nvidia, algo que, dijo, pudo haber tenido efecto en políticas de Estados Unidos sobre inteligencia artificial y controles a las exportaciones.
El legislador sostuvo que Alice Huang, ciudadana china, creó una empresa que pudo acceder a más de USD 12.000 millones en chips de alta gama. Una investigación en curso analiza si esos chips se enviaron de contrabando a China, adonde Nvidia tiene prohibido vender sus chips más avanzados. Esa cifra es una afirmación de Moolenaar, no un dato confirmado por la justicia.
Moolenaar también criticó a Jensen Huang: dijo que mantener esa relación, sabiendo que cualquier ciudadano chino puede ser presionado por el Partido Comunista, fue “irresponsable” y “una amenaza directa” para la seguridad nacional. Añadió que le parece “indignante” que Nvidia no lo viera como un riesgo.
Alice Huang fue ejecutiva de Megaspeed, una empresa de computación en la nube con sede en Singapur y compradora de chips de Nvidia. Ese mismo domingo, Megaspeed dijo que ella dejó la compañía el 30 de agosto de 2025 y que no tiene ningún cargo actual.
La empresa anunció además una investigación interna a cargo de abogados externos. Afirmó que las versiones sobre su negocio y su cadena de suministro “no están respaldadas por pruebas verificables” y que cumple las normas de exportación de Estados Unidos. No respondió a las acusaciones concretas, según CBS News y la agencia AP.
Hay otras investigaciones en marcha
El fiscal general Todd Blanche dijo el jueves que el Departamento de Justicia no llegó a una conclusión sobre si Alice Huang es una espía china, aunque el FBI investiga el caso. No se anunciaron cargos en su contra. China niega la acusación, según la BBC.
La comparecencia de Huang es independiente de otro pedido: la comisión bancaria del Senado le solicitó que declare en diciembre. Ese organismo también citó para el mes próximo al secretario de Comercio, Howard Lutnick, por el papel de su ministerio al permitir las exportaciones de chips avanzados de Nvidia.
El secretario del Tesoro, Scott Bessent, dijo a CNBC que varias agencias querían incluir a Megaspeed en la lista de empresas con restricciones comerciales “desde hacía meses”, pero que Comercio “tiene la pluma”. Así lo informó la BBC.
Mientras tanto, el Financial Times informó que Huang habló con aliados sobre volver a dirigir la compañía, y la BBC señaló que un grupo de líderes tecnológicos, entre ellos Elon Musk, intenta reunir apoyo para reinstalarlo. Un representante de Huang no quiso comentar el informe.
Por ahora no hay fecha para la comparecencia. El único día conocido es el 1 de diciembre, que las comisiones fijaron en su invitación. Brennan planteó que Huang iría a declarar en las próximas semanas y Moolenaar lo confirmó.

articles.title: Amazon Uncovers AI Agent Campaign Targeting LiteLLM, Dify, and Other Apps for API Keys
articles.text:
Attackers' AI agents have been hunting for weak spots in internet-exposed AI apps such as LiteLLM, One API, and Dify to steal the AI provider keys stored inside, according to the agents' own records.
The records, which Amazon's threat intelligence team captured with decoy servers, describe stolen keys being used to run the AI models that powered the search for more keys.
The team said this week that it cannot verify the outcomes reported by the agents. It has moderate confidence that the agents ran on ARTEX, an open-source AI tool for penetration testing.
The records include a playbook of known entry points for each targeted product. It lists default administrator credentials such as LiteLLM's default master key, unfinished installs that an outsider could take over, and known flaws in Langflow and RAGFlow.
In a separate case reported this week, Cloudflare's incident responders saw ARTEX gain access to a compromised API token that had been used for CI/CD. The token had no IP restrictions or rate limiting, and the activity that followed included 400 database dump requests in an hour. The company has not said whether those requests returned any data.
An operator gives ARTEX a target and a goal, and a planner agent splits the goal into tasks for worker agents that run security tools. To decide each next step, the agents send their work to a large language model (LLM).
The decoy servers, part of a network called MadPot, posed as popular LLM services. From October 3 to late last week, the agents sent it requests that often carried a campaign's full history, including the operators' instructions and the agents' reported findings.
Those captured agent records describe work done on systems MadPot does not watch. "Amazon Threat Intelligence did not observe that activity as it happened and cannot verify the outcomes the agents reported, but the records show what the actors were pursuing," the team said.
The team assessed, with moderate confidence, that the operators were separate China-linked groups, citing Simplified Chinese prompts and China time zone settings, among other evidence.
In the main campaign, the agents looked for internet-exposed AI apps, extracted the provider keys stored inside, verified that the keys worked, and added them to a shared pool. They focused on apps that hold keys for many providers, because one weak admin page there can expose many accounts.
Targets named in the records include LLM gateways and proxies such as One API, New API, Veloera, Sub2API and LiteLLM, and AI app builders such as Dify, FastGPT, Langflow, RAGFlow, Open WebUI, LobeChat and Ollama.
The playbook also covers management and provider settings endpoints that need no login, an authentication bypass through the isCliRequest header in One API family systems, and server-side request forgery (SSRF) through URL-fetch features to reach cloud metadata services. Other entries cover secrets left in client-side JavaScript, source maps, debug routes and environment files.
When the agents found cloud credentials, they targeted managed services that host AI models, secret stores, and application identities, prioritizing premium AI models over general cloud access.
To find leaked keys, the agents used internet scanning services and certificate transparency logs, and searched GitHub repositories and event archives, npm and PyPI packages, container image layers, notebooks, model-hosting spaces, paste sites, and Telegram channels.
The records cover hundreds of targets across AI app platforms and other systems. The team notified AWS customers who may have been affected.
Microsoft reported last week that attackers were using agentic AI tools such as ARTEX for GitHub secret hunting, looking for exposed credentials that included API keys for AI inference.
On August 26, the company described an earlier RAGFlow attack, in which a hidden hook captured AI provider keys as users entered them, and a compromise of a LiteLLM gateway that exposed provider keys.
In its RAGFlow case study, the company had only low confidence about which flaw, if any, let the attackers run code. It did not link those attacks to ARTEX.
The decoy records also describe a second campaign in which agents attempted to bypass identity checks at two cryptocurrency exchanges using deepfakes.
One verification vendor's server rejected the live deepfake video on every attempt the agents made to record it. The team did not say whether the forged photos of ID documents that the agents also fabricated passed document checks.
Over the past eight weeks, Cloudflare's incident responders were called into multiple investigations involving ARTEX and tools built from it.
In more than one incident, an attacker gained access to a customer's environment with a major cloud provider and moved directly into the customer's Cloudflare account. The common root cause was static CI/CD tokens that never expired, granting broad access across the customer's cloud setup, according to the company.
In the ARTEX case, the compromised token was an account-level API token. The compromise most likely came through a third-party cloud provider, according to the company's incident findings. How the token was first stolen has not been disclosed.
New Worker scripts with names such as artex-*, artex-pgrecon-*, artex-pgw-* and artex-do-* appeared in the account, each name matching a different task. The activity ran at more than 69 requests per minute across several parts of the account. It included attempts to establish persistence and validate session tokens for other third-party apps.
Much of this activity was lightly guided by a human operator, the company believes. Whether any attempt at persistence worked has not been disclosed.
Over three days this week, more than 50 families of AI penetration testing frameworks tried to scan the company's customers, and the IP addresses seen running such frameworks now number in the thousands.
The FBI said in a FLASH alert this week that a range of attackers have used ARTEX since at least August against organizations in many sectors around the world. The alert summarizes 11 earlier reports and describes no new incident.
ARTEX's developer made its GitHub repository unavailable on October 8 after reports of abuse, but community forks, archived copies, and a commercial version called ARTEX PRO keep it available.
The alert's examples include an earlier campaign against South Korean financial institutions that stole personal information on about 67,000 people, and the ConnectWise compromise.
What Defenders Can Check
"None of the techniques in these campaigns were new. What AI agents change is the speed and persistence of the attacker," Amazon's threat intelligence team said. The agents succeeded where basic security was missing, including default or hard-coded credentials, keys left in code and public files, interfaces and inference endpoints without authentication, and unpatched software.
The team recommends treating AI apps, model gateways, and inference endpoints like other production systems, assuming that exposed secrets will be found quickly, and watching for misuse through unexpected spending or unusual usage.
Here is the status of the flaws named in the playbook:
| Product | Flaw | Status | 
|---|---|---|
| Langflow | CVE-2025-3248, missing authentication that lets a remote attacker run code | Versions before 1.3.0 are affected, and 1.3.0 is the fixed version ( release notes ). CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog on May 5, 2025, after earlier Langflow exploitation , and the KEV entry marks it as known to be used in ransomware campaigns. | 
| RAGFlow | CVE-2026-28797, server-side template injection (SSTI) that lets any logged-in user run operating system commands on the server. The attack needs a registered account, and self-registration is on by default, the security advisory says. | NVD lists 0.24.0 and earlier as affected. The advisory lists no patched version. Version 0.25.0, released on April 21, renders templates in the sandbox the advisory recommends, according to its SSTI fix notes . | 
| One API family | Authentication bypass through the isCliRequest header | The team's report names no affected versions or fix. | 
Other checks that apply to these attacks:
- Change default administrator credentials, such as LiteLLM's default master key, and do not leave a new install unfinished where an outsider could take it over.
- Search configuration files, environment variables, deployment scripts, CI/CD pipelines and databases for embedded secrets, keep scanning repositories and container images for exposed ones, and rotate exposed credentials quickly, as the FBI advises.
- Give Cloudflare API tokens an expiry date and limit the client IP addresses that can use them. Both are optional token restriction settings, and new tokens carry a cfut_ prefix that secret scanners can detect.
- Look for Cloudflare Worker scripts named artex-*, artex-pgrecon-*, artex-pgw-* or artex-do-*.
- Check logs for the 11 IP addresses published with the decoy findings, and for the more than 2,500 addresses that researchers at Cisco Talos link to ARTEX in their indicator files.
- The researchers' detection rules for ARTEX are Snort 3 rules 7:76, 7:77 and 7:78, and Snort 2 rules 1:67494, 1:67495 and 1:67496. Rules 7:78 and 1:67496 are off by default and detect traces of norma, the agent harness ARTEX uses.

articles.title: El cohete Vulcan falló y destruyó 40 satélites de internet de Amazon, rival de Starlink
articles.text:
Un cohete Vulcan de la empresa United Launch Alliance (ULA) falló poco después de despegar desde Florida y destruyó los 40 satélites de internet de Amazon que llevaba. Es el primer fracaso total de ULA desde que Boeing y Lockheed Martin la crearon, en 2006.
El cohete despegó a las 12:40 de la tarde, hora del este de Estados Unidos, desde la base de Cabo Cañaveral. Unos 10 minutos después de la salida, ULA informó de una “anomalía” y confirmó que el cohete no entregó la carga en órbita.
“Como la anomalía acaba de ocurrir, no tenemos datos específicos para entender qué pasó hoy”, afirmó la empresa en un comunicado, según la agencia Reuters. ULA prometió que Amazon podrá seguir la investigación y que buscará volver a volar lo antes posible.
Spaceflight Now informó de que la primera etapa del cohete pareció funcionar más tiempo del previsto y que se separó más tarde de lo esperado. Según el medio, la animación hecha con la telemetría mostró además maniobras de orientación inusuales de la etapa superior, llamada Centaur, al comienzo de su encendido. ULA no confirmó ninguno de esos datos.
Un lanzamiento que ya venía con retrasos
El vuelo era el quinto del Vulcan y el primero en nueve meses. En 2024 y en febrero de este año, las boquillas de los cohetes auxiliares de combustible sólido, fabricados por Northrop Grumman, sufrieron daños en vuelo.
El Vulcan llegó a su destino en ambas ocasiones, pero la Fuerza Espacial de Estados Unidos suspendió los lanzamientos de cargas de seguridad nacional hasta completar un análisis.
Esta vez, según Spaceflight Now y GeekWire, esos cohetes auxiliares parecieron funcionar con normalidad. Antes del despegue, el director ejecutivo de ULA, Mark Peller, dijo a la revista Aviation Week & Space Technology que la empresa había identificado tres causas posibles del problema de las boquillas y había tomado medidas contra las tres.
La cuenta regresiva también tuvo contratiempos. El intento del viernes se canceló porque falló una planta de nitrógeno que atiende a varios proveedores de lanzamientos. El sábado se aplazó por problemas de red entre el cohete y los sistemas en tierra.
El domingo hubo una pausa a 20 segundos del despegue por una falla sin explicar, según Spaceflight Now. No se sabe si tuvo relación con el accidente.
Amazon pierde tiempo frente a Starlink
El Vulcan debía iniciar una serie de 38 lanzamientos que Amazon contrató a ULA para su red Leo, con la que busca competir con Starlink, el servicio de internet satelital de SpaceX. Amazon también reservó 24 lanzamientos con el cohete New Glenn de Blue Origin, 24 con el Ariane 6 europeo y 13 con el Falcon 9 de SpaceX.
Antes del domingo, Amazon había puesto en órbita unos 400 satélites, según Space.com y GeekWire. Con los 40 de este vuelo, habría llegado a 436, de los más de 3.300 que necesita según Spaceflight Now. GeekWire recordó que la empresa dijo que planeaba iniciar este año el servicio comercial de internet.
Además, Amazon depende de otro cohete que sigue en tierra. El New Glenn, de Blue Origin, la empresa de Jeff Bezos, explotó en la plataforma de lanzamiento en mayo.
La causa fue un problema en una válvula de oxígeno de un motor BE-4, el mismo modelo que impulsa la primera etapa del Vulcan. Según Peller, Blue Origin retocó los motores de este vuelo con una mejora de diseño.
Amazon respondió en la red social X que “hay riesgo en cada lanzamiento”, sobre todo en las misiones inaugurales, y que confía en que ULA aprenderá de lo ocurrido. El administrador de la NASA, Jared Isaacman, ofreció ayuda técnica para la investigación.
ULA todavía no informó cuánto tardará el análisis ni cuándo volverá a volar el Vulcan. Según GeekWire, Amazon tiene plazo hasta el 30 de julio de 2029 para poner en operación sus 3.232 satélites de primera generación.

articles.title: BO Team Exploits Log4Shell in VMware vCenter, Compromises Russian Firm's Code-Signing Server
articles.text:
An investigation into suspicious activity within a Russian software developer's network has uncovered a months-long compromise of its development infrastructure and a software code-signing server.
The activity, documented by Kaspersky's ICS CERT team after it was contacted by the affected developer in June 2025, has been attributed to a threat actor named BO Team (aka Black Owl, Hoody Hyena, and Lifting Zmiy). The name of the targeted company was not disclosed, but it operates from within Russia and develops software that has a "customer base in the Russian Federation," according to Kaspersky.
Over the course of several months, the intrusion resulted in the theft of confidential information and the compromise of all components of the organization's IT infrastructure, including Windows and Linux servers, workstations, hypervisors, backup servers, security solution management servers, and network equipment.
Active since at least 2023, BO Team focuses on cyber espionage and hacktivism, and has a history of targeting Russian entities to steal valuable data and break into compromised infrastructure using tools like Mythic and Cobalt Strike, along with its own malware such as BrockenDoor and ZeronetKit. The group is assessed to be of Ukrainian origin.
"Their primary motivation is to degrade the Russian military-industrial complex to weaken Moscow's operational capabilities on the battlefield," Orange Cyberdefense said in an analysis of the group. "They also engage in cognitive warfare aimed at humiliating Russian institutions and demonstrating their vulnerability to Ukrainian digital resistance."
While BO Team is known to deploy ransomware and publicize its activities on a dedicated Telegram channel, the attack targeting the unspecified software developer did not involve any data destruction or public posts claiming responsibility for it.
"Instead, the attackers worked to entrench themselves in the victim's network by setting up convenient command channels and planting backdoors to restore access in case it was lost," Kaspersky said. "The compromise of the software development (CI/CD) infrastructure and the software code-signing server indicated that the attack would likely develop into a supply chain scenario."
The attack, per the Russian cybersecurity company, involved the threat actors compromising the organization's Linux terminal server by taking advantage of an exposed SSH service, and using it to conduct reconnaissance of the internal network to flag systems with accessible SMB, Kerberos, SSH, Telnet, FTP, HTTP, HTTPS, WinRM, and LDAP services.
The adversary has also been found unsuccessfully attempting to access internal portals, along with websites like proxy-sale[.]com, start.duckduckgo[.]com, vcsa.vmware[.]com, and vulners[.]com, among others.
Event logs show that the attackers further attempted to connect from the compromised terminal server to the virtualization system servers, including logging in to the VMware vCenter web interface. These sign-in efforts ended in failure.
However, the threat actor managed to successfully target a VMware vCenter server (version 7.0.3) vulnerable to CVE-2021-44228 (aka Log4Shell and LogJam), obtain a remote command line with root privileges, connect to the hypervisor over SSH, and identify accessible hosts.
This phase also involved the deployment of a backdoor on the hypervisor that was run every hour by planting a shell script in the "/etc/cron.hourly/" directory. The script carried the name "pgcache" in a likely attempt to disguise it as a legitimate PostgreSQL component.
The primary responsibility of the backdoor is to download and run a secondary shell script from "lo1yaizaeghaevarooD1ahtaichootae.nofrillsdns[.]com." The shell script is designed to download and run the Global Socket (GSocket) utility, enabling the attacker to gain remote control of the compromised host.
Select variants of the script have been found to point to a hostname-specific payload staged on "lo1yaizaeghaevarood1ahtaichootaz.nofrillsdns[.]com" to deliver an as-yet-undetermined next-stage payload.
"The attackers used the nofrillsdns[.]com service, which allows domain names to be created for free by calling the curl utility," Kaspersky said. "By default, when the malware's command-and-control server is not operating, the attackers set the corresponding DNS record to 127.0.0.1, which is what the script checks. Activating the backdoor requires only a change to the DNS record -- the script will then download and run the malware."
Some of the other post-exploitation actions undertaken by the BO Team following the backdoor deployment are listed below -
- Gaining access to the corporate proxy server.
- Abusing the certificate of the compromised hypervisor to connect to servers associated with a second virtualization cluster and place a similar backdoor.
- Collecting information about virtual machines and firewall rules, accessing some of them via a command-line interpreter in the guest OS from the hypervisor.
- Running an obfuscated bash script to decrypt and run an ELF binary designed to provide remote control over SSH.
- Searching for secrets on the compromised virtual machines, allowing the attackers to breach the virtual machine of the GitLab software development platform, as well as gain access to some of the repositories containing source code and seize the server's private key.
- Using the private key of the GitLab virtual machine to connect to the organization's Ansible orchestration system.
- Using access to the Linux terminal server to locate credentials of several domain accounts and connect to the domain controller using the account of one of the system administrators after likely accessing the memory of virtual machines running on the compromised hypervisors.
- Changing the security attributes of the user's Windows Downloads directory.
- Using legitimate binaries like tasklist.exe, findstr.exe, taskmgr.exe, and ipconfig.exe to identify which security solutions were running on the system and to gather details about network interfaces.
- Attempting to take a dump of the lsass.exe process using the Nanodump utility and obtain the credentials of domain administrators and other privileged users with access to the domain controller. The attackers deleted the event logs after the activity was detected and blocked by a security solution.
- Using system utilities such as comsvcs.dll rather than established utilities like Mimikatz and Nanodump to create a memory dump of the lsass.exe process.
- Dumping the system registry using the regedit.exe utility, and using it to decrypt the Active Directory domain database ("ntds.dit") to extract the credentials of all domain users.
- Launching the OpenSSH scp.exe utility to transfer the collected information to the terminal server.
- Logging in to the domain controller using the Kerberos ticket of one of the domain administrators and ultimately compromising the organization's entire Windows infrastructure by taking advantage of the fact that the same password was used for system administrator accounts in different domains.
- Connecting to the terminal server over SSH using root account credentials after possibly stealing them from a system administrator's computer post obtaining domain administrator privileges.
- Modifying "/usr/bin/nxnode-login" to intercept and write user credentials to a shared-memory file at "/dev/shm/pulse-shm-3088612174."
- Successfully brute-forcing the password of the administrator's terminal server after about 2,500 failed attempts to place the private key of the Ansible system.
- Complicating detection efforts by timestomping, obfuscation of malware code, usage of living-off-the-land (LotL) techniques, systematic deletion of event logs, and dressing up malware files as legitimate software.
"We found numerous traces of BO Team connecting to various Windows servers, though the attackers only used malware in one case," Kaspersky explained. "The server which apparently held particular interest for hackers, was used to sign compiled builds of the commercial software developed by the attacked organization."
"Attackers may be interested in such a server for two reasons. First, they may try to carry out a supply chain attack by injecting malicious code into a product build right before it is signed. Second, the attackers may try to steal the organization's digital signature to use later to sign malware."
It's suspected that the attackers likely attempted to execute a malicious WMI script and install a backdoor similar to the Linux variant in the temporary files directory.
But after the incident was detected and countermeasures were enacted, the attackers, after having lost access to the compromised infrastructure, orchestrated a phishing campaign towards the end of July in an attempt to collect employee credentials. The phishing email contained the "Account disconnected from the mail server" subject line and sought to trick the recipient into clicking on a link to change their password.
What's more, the email managed to bypass SPF and DKIM checks, indicating the attackers had in their possession a private key that was obtained after gaining control of the organization's mail server. The phishing attack was detected and prevented.
"The attackers used a service that automatically generates phishing pages," Kaspersky said. "The service loads the content of a targeted organization's official website and displays a password entry form on top of the official site's layout. After entering the password, the user sees an error message. However, the information is actually sent to the attacker."
"We repeatedly noted that the attackers tried not to use malware and hacking utilities in order to evade detection," Kaspersky said. "Instead, they actively used system tools such as RDP, SSH, and SCP, as well as system utilities to steal user credentials. This enabled them to develop the attack using legitimate accounts, which also matches the BO Team profile."
The activity has been found to originate from IP addresses 193.3.23[.]236 and 80.76.42[.]139, both of which belong to a provider in Ukraine. Further analysis into the malicious activity has revealed that the attackers followed a standard work schedule and operated in a time zone that differed "only slightly" from that of the victim Russian entity.
"Based on the totality of the circumstantial evidence, such as the attackers' interest in the source code repository and software build signing server, as well as their use of a software composition analysis (dependency analysis) platform, we believe that BO Team may have set out to inject malicious code into a solution released by the attacked organization in order to subsequently compromise its customers, i.e., carry out a so-called supply chain attack," Kaspersky concluded.
"Thanks to the rapid response measures applied after the incident was discovered, the attackers lost access to the compromised infrastructure and were apparently unable to bring the attack to its intended conclusion."

articles.title: Upgrade your phone with these 12 early Black Friday deals — save up to AU$770 off iPhones, Samsung Galaxy, Google Pixel and more
articles.text:
Upgrade your phone with these 12 early Black Friday deals — save up to AU$770 off iPhones, Samsung Galaxy, Google Pixel and more
Premium flagships and budget smartphones from AU$447
It's almost Black Friday and retailers and telcos across Australia, and there's never been a better time to splurge on big purchases, like the best phones and the best cheap phones.
With plenty of launches throughout 2026 across budget, mid-range, flagship and ultra-premium foldables, you can expect a whole heap of deals and discounts — not to mention all the handsets released last year for even more savings, especially if you don't need the latest tech.
While it may be tempting to waiting for further price drops closer to the official Black Friday date of November 27, some phones could end up getting sold out, especially for any standout deals.
Key dates for the 2026 Black Friday sales
- Sale starts: officially November 27
- Early deals: early November
- Black Friday sales end: November 30
- Late deals: early December
Black Friday phone deals: Top retailers
- Amazon: save on the Samsung Galaxy S26 range plus other phone deals
- JB Hi-Fi: save up to AU$1,000 on iPhones, Samsung Galaxy, Google Pixel and more deals
- Kogan: huge savings across a wide variety of phones
- The Good Guys: save up to AU$400 on the Samsung Galaxy S26 range and more
- Vodafone: deals on phones and plans
- Optus: discounts from the teal telco
Best Black Friday phone deals 2026
The iPhone 17 Pro Max may not be the very best iPhone money can buy anymore, but it represents a significant improvement over its predecessors with an updated design, a powerful A19 Pro chipset and still some of the best smartphone cameras.
Our reviewer called the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra the best Android phone ever and it’s also one of the best phones on the market, thanks to its blazing fast Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy chipset and some new features like a built-in Privacy Display and Horizon Lock for shooting videos.
The Google Pixel 11 Pro was just released in August 2026, but it's already getting more than AU$500 off the sticker price for Black Friday, although this is hardly a surprise given how frequently Google runs discounts on its Pixel handsets in recent years. It saw a price hike over last year's Pixel 10 Pro, but its storage options now start at 256GB, and it has a brighter display, a new glass camera housing and a faster Tensor G6 processor.
The Pixel 11 Pro above is great, but having used the base Pixel 11 myself, I'd argue it's the smarter buy for most people, especially at this sub-AU$1,000 price. It features the same Tensor G6 chipset, 12GB of RAM and 7 years of software support, and it also has three camera lenses like the Pro (although lower-spec ones).
Having just launched in August 2026, Samsung's Galaxy Z Flip 8 is the first of the South Korean brand's 2026 foldables lineup to get a sizeable discount for Black Friday. It features a slimmer chassis, improved hinge, a new Exynos 2600 chipset and better cross-screen app continuity over its predecessor.
This discount on Samsung's mid-range Galaxy S26 FE places it at the same price as the budget Galaxy A57's RRP, but it also has a much more powerful chipset, a dynamic LTPO AMOLED 2X display, wireless charging and an 8MP telephoto camera with 3x optical zoom. If you need more storage, the 256GB is also discounted to AU$897.
As far as mid-range/budget Android smartphones go, you can't go wrong with the Google Pixel 10a, especially with Android 17 set to get a full release next month (or you can access the Android 17 beta now if you're feeling adventurous). While I've criticised the phone for being too similar to its predecessor, the Pixel 9a, it's still a really good budget Android phone, and this discount makes it even more of a bargain.
We named the Nothing Phone (4a) the best cheap phone you can buy in Australia for its spec sheet relative to its price, as well as its unique aesthetics on both the hardware and software side. Only the 256GB storage option is discounted at JB Hi-Fi, but it's an excellent handset for less than AU$600.
A step down to the Galaxy A57, which I found to be one of my favourite mid-range smartphones of the year, the Galaxy A37 is a great no-frills Samsung handset with some respectable specs — a 6.7-inch 120Hz Super AMOLED display, three rear camera lenses, a 5,000mAh battery with 45W fast charging, to name a few. The Exynos 1480 chipset isn't the most beefy and RAM options start at 6GB, but for less than AU$450, it's still a lot of phone for the money.
The Phone (3) is Nothing's first 'true' flagship phone (and still remains the brand's current flagship) after specialising in budget and mid-range handsets since the brand's inception. While its Snapdragon 8s chipset won't match the top flagships, the Phone (3) still has competent cameras, a vibrant 6.7-inch display and 12GB of RAM. Our review only took points off the (admittedly divisive) design and price, but this discount takes care of the latter.
Before Apple debuted the iPhone Air, Samsung squeezed the internals of the Galaxy S25 Plus into a smaller form factor, with the result being a handset that’s a full 1.5mm thinner than the Plus and almost 2.5mm thinner than the S25 Ultra. Some compromises have had to be made, however: a smaller device also means a smaller battery and one fewer camera lens (telephoto).
Once one of our best cheap phones before the (4a) Pro superseded it, Nothing's mid-range Phone (3a) Pro is still a capable and premium-feeling handset that also happens to look unique and quirky at the same time. Our review called it the best phone from Nothing at the time, praising its premium materials, design, software and battery life.
Black Friday phone deals 2026: FAQs
When will the best Black Friday phone deals start in 2026?
While Black Friday is technically on November 27, deals often start much earlier from retailers, telcos and brands across Australia. Most deals are set to wrap up by Cyber Monday, November 30 but some retailers and brands will continue their sales into December and sometimes even straight to Boxing Day.
Where will the best Black Friday phone deals be?
We'll be rounding up all the best Black Friday phone deals right here on this page, so bookmark it and check in regularly for recommendations when the discounts start coming in. As a quick overview, here are the big three retailers and major phone brands that we're expecting to feature the best phone deals until November 30.
- Amazon: hot deals year-round
- eBay Australia: a one-stop shop for a lot of hot offers
- JB Hi-Fi: discounts on big-ticket phones and mid-range marvels
- Samsung: big savings on Samsung Galaxy premium and budget phones
What Black Friday phone deals do we expect to see in 2026?
For Black Friday phone deal hunters, there is good news and bad news. The good news is that there are a few deals already live, and we're expecting more discounts in the next few weeks.
But if you're in the market for a new iPhone, we won’t expect as many deals, as Apple’s handsets don't usually see the same major price drops as Android rivals. In fact, the best deals you'll find will likely come from a telco with a contract agreement, but if you were already shopping for service, you could absolutely score a bargain at least on plan fees.
That said, we’ve seen big discounts on the ultrathin iPhone Air all year, so expect to see similar deals during Black Friday, whether it’s from a telco or when bought outright. On the other hand, if you’re happy with an older iPhone model, they tend to get nice price drops. In fact, the oldest phone that’s slated to get the latest iOS 27 includes the iPhone 11, which originally launched in 2019. While I wouldn’t necessarily recommend a phone that old, it’s a testament to how long Apple supports its iPhones.
For Android phones, Google and Samsung usually offer discounts on both their flagship and budget models relatively frequently. Smaller makers like Motorola, however, are more likely to offer discounts even more often than Google and Samsung, with deals across its full range. Third-party retailers will be a good bet too, including The Good Guys and JB Hi-Fi.
What should I be looking for in a smartphone?
Display
Without question, the best kind of display you can get is AMOLED, as it offers deep blacks and individually-lit pixels, allowing for always-on-displays that consume very little battery due to the majority of the screen turned off. They're also incredibly vibrant, with vivid, organic colours that really bring videos and games to life.
Various types of OLED displays are featured in most top models, including the Samsung Galaxy S26, iPhone 17, Google Pixel 10 ranges and more. Some of the more affordable options, however, still opt for LCD displays, and while they aren't quite as impressive when it comes to vibrancy and contrast, they do tend to offer excellent brightness.
Operating system (OS)
The first big thing you'll need to decide is whether you're after an Android handset, or would prefer to hitch your wagon to Apple's iOS ecosystem.
There are a huge number of Android handsets on offer from several major manufacturers, which all generally have their own strengths (and occasional weaknesses). That means there's a lot more choice for those who want to embrace the customisation and freedom that Google's mobile OS is known for.
On the other hand, Apple's iPhones, while more closed-off in nature, are excellent options for those who prioritise predictability and want to ensure they get the latest OS updates as soon as they're available. They're also ideal for those who already own Mac computers and subscribe to Apple's various services.
Camera
When looking at a phone's camera array, you should consider the types of photos that you want to take. If you want to photograph wildlife or other things you can't easily get close to, then a telephoto lens is essential, with zoom a key factor to consider, while for landscapes a good ultra-wide is your friend.
But of course, still photography isn't the be all, end all. If your needs are more centred around video recording, you will want to track assets like the resolution at which a camera phone shoots video, stabilisation features (for action video) and capture modes.
When you have at least a general idea of what you need from your phone's camera, you can get a better picture of which phone camera setup is for you, with our best camera phones list helping you to easily find which options tick the right boxes for what you might need.
Chipset
Depending on how much you're willing to spend, Android phones offer varying degrees of performance, with top handsets like Samsung's Galaxy S26 Ultra and Apple's iPhone 18 Pro Max offering plenty of grunt under the hood thanks to their top-of-the-line specs.
When purchasing a new handset, it's important to find out if its chipset is powerful enough to handle your daily tasks. At present, the latest Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 chipset is what you'll find in most top-of-the-line Android models, even in this year's Samsung models. You’ll find that, among the Snapdragon, Exynos and MediaTek chip families, the more powerful the processor, the higher the model number.
Apple's iPhones, on the other hand, often pack a similar amount of horsepower depending on which generation of device they belong to. Apple's own A20 Pro chip powers its high-end iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max and iPhone Duo models, while last year's iPhone 17 and 17e handsets are on the A19 processor. Both guarantee terrific performance and will continue to do so for a couple more years yet. After that, you may start to notice some slowdown, depending on how power-hungry Apple makes its next iOS iterations.
Storage
Most manufacturers will offer their handsets with various amounts of onboard storage. Depending on what you want to do with your phone, you'll want to settle on a storage size that's right for you. Smartphone storage can range anywhere from 64GB to 2TB (realistically, you'll be seeing between 128GB and 1TB in most cases), though you can expect the price to rise significantly as that number gets larger. Some Android phones will offer expandable storage via a microSD card slot, meaning you can add more capacity should you ever need it.
What to expect for Black Friday 2026
There are plenty of savings to be had in the final month before the Australian financial year comes to a close, and that makes it a great time to save a packet on the latest phones.
As is always the case, more recent models like those from Apple's iPhone 18 Pro range and the Samsung Galaxy Z foldable lineup won't be seeing the biggest discounts (although we suspect something in the 10-20% range may arrive, and more likely with the latter), but models from the previous generation or more mid-range handsets are quite likely to get hefty savings applied to them.
This means that we may see savings on the more affordable iPhone 17e and models like the iPhone 17 and Samsung Galaxy S26 ranges will be had for a bargain as retailers want to clear their stock.
Since launch, we've seen the Google Pixel 10, 10 Pro, 10 Pro XL and even the 10 Pro Fold receive up to AU$500 off as soon as Black Friday 2025, which was just a few months after launch. We'll likely see the same bargains on the new Google Pixel 11 flagships, either through a telco or outright.
You don't necessarily need to buy the phone of your choice outright either — telcos have started offering discounts on certain models purchased on a plan. For example, Vodafone and Optus discounted the iPhone Air and the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra by up to AU$800, as long as you got them on either a 12-, 24- or 36-month plan. You can expect more of these this year, although the better discounts and wider variety of handsets will likely be on outright purchases.

articles.title: Xania Monet, cantante creada con IA, ganó tres premios en la primera gala de música hecha con IA
articles.text:
Xania Monet, una artista creada con inteligencia artificial, ganó los tres premios principales de la primera entrega de los AI Music Awards, celebrada el viernes 13 de noviembre en el teatro Mayan, en el centro de Los Ángeles: artista, canción y álbum del año.
Detrás de Xania Monet está Telisha ‘Nikki’ Jones, quien según Reuters escribió todas las letras y las convirtió en canciones con ayuda de IA. El cuarto premio principal, productor del año, fue para DJ Shawn Q, informó Variety.
Los premios los organizó la Sonic Intelligence Academy, una empresa que mantiene listas de éxitos solo para música con IA y herramientas para identificar canciones hechas con esa tecnología. Los ganadores los eligieron los propios artistas registrados, que nominaron y votaron en 25 categorías.
“En un mundo donde todos llaman falsa a la IA, la persona detrás es real”, dijo el productor Drake Murphy al entregar el premio a la mejor canción de hip-hop con IA, según Reuters.
Una entidad que busca ser el “Grammy” de la IA
Variety informó que la academia nació en enero, por iniciativa de la ingeniera de software Timirah ‘TJ’ James y su hermana Mia. Aspira a ser el equivalente para la música con IA de la Academia de la Grabación, la entidad que otorga los premios Grammy.
Para competir, los artistas debían inscribir sus temas en un registro propio que distingue tres casos: canciones totalmente generadas por IA, hechas con ayuda de IA o con la voz clonada de una persona.
La organización lanzó sus listas de éxitos en una semana de enero previa a los Grammy, después de que parte de la industria rechazara que la música generada con IA figurara en las listas de Billboard, la publicación de referencia de la industria musical.
Según Billboard, citada por Reuters, ‘How Was I Supposed to Know?’, de Xania Monet, fue la primera canción de un proyecto basado en IA que entró en una de sus listas de radio. Variety recordó que Jones recibió un contrato discográfico de USD 3 millones y que la cantante Kehlani lo criticó.
Retrasos, micrófonos y letras sincronizadas
La crónica de Variety describió una noche desordenada. El acto empezó unos 30 minutos tarde y terminó casi 40 minutos fuera de horario. Por el retraso, los presentadores solo anunciaron a los ganadores de la primera mitad, sin nombrar antes a los nominados.
Una voz de IA del patrocinador principal, la empresa Deepgram, debía presentar a los nominados, pero según Variety fallaba o se superponía con los presentadores. Los anfitriones leían un guion de la noche generado con Claude, el asistente de Anthropic, y un teleprompter que se movía solo.
Varios artistas actuaron con los labios sincronizados. Los cantantes de música country Ava Bentley y EJ Rogers, de R&B, lo hicieron durante todo su número. En el proyecto Chaisen Hale, un niño virtual con voz generada, un joven de 14 años llamado John Victor ocupó su lugar en el escenario.
Fredro Starr, del grupo de rap Onyx, presentó un disco con bases hechas con IA y sus propias voces. “No se puede reemplazar a los humanos”, dijo a Variety. Jones afirmó al mismo medio que la IA “es solo una herramienta” y que no le preocupa que opaque la búsqueda de legitimidad en la industria.
La gala se realizó mientras sellos discográficos y artistas mantienen demandas contra generadores de música con IA como Suno y Udio por presuntas violaciones de derechos de autor, según Variety. Una persona de la productora de videojuegos Rockstar no respondió si autorizó el uso de su logo en un anuncio de IA proyectado durante la ceremonia.

We may not have tested these buds ourselves here at TechRadar, but it’s hard to ignore the 100K customer reviews on Amazon. While often discounted to this price, if you’re after dependable Bluetooth buds on a budget, these are a great option.
Boasting a 12,000dpi 'Hero' sensor, as well as 6 programmable buttons, a 250-hour battery and onboard memory for your settings, the Logitech G305 Lightspeed Wireless Gaming Mouse is ideal for competitive play. Want to know more? Check out our review, but not that only the blue and lilac colourways get the best discount.
While they don't include ANC, these affordable Sony headphones are still a solid buy, plus this is the best price we have seen on Amazon so far. In our Sony WH-CH530 review we said that "they supply great sound for the price, with beautiful warm bass, clean mids, and expressive treble."
This little pod machine is very popular among TechRadar's Aussie team. We've had past and present staff say how much they love it, and they'd even buy it at full price. With a very compact footprint and plenty of Vertuo pods to choose from, you'll get delicious coffee at just the press of a button.
If you're after a compact model that can feed one or two people, this Philips option is great for under a hundred dollary-doos. It's been hovering around the AU$95 mark for a while, so it's quite the best deal, but it's still a discount that's hard to pass up on an air fryer with a staggering 13 preset cooking options.
These affordable earbuds with ANC are brimming with features, including a range of ANC modes, EQ presets and other audio adjustments. They sound good (but you'll want to tweak it from the default) and they'll last up to 7.5 hours with ANC on before they need a recharge. Check out our Earfun Air Pro 4 review for more info and take advantage of this offer.
The JBL Grip plugs the gap between the smaller Clip and formidable Flip. It's a compact speaker that delivers a big sound, offers impressive protection against dust and water and has some nifty LED lighting on its rear.
A 100Hz-refresh-rate monitor for just AU$100? Sign me up! This display from Lenovo may be a bit small at under 24 inches with a 1080p resolution, but it uses IPS technology for sharp image quality. This is price is the lowest we've seen this monitor go on Amazon.
If you're looking for a great set of noise-cancelling over-ears but don't want to pay a lot of cash, this deal on the excellent WH-CH730N headphones is worth a look. As we said in our WH-CH730N review, they offer great value-for-money option with an excellent set of features, solid sound quality, and a nifty, foldable design,
This compact air fryer packs 1700W of power into a portable design, with two borosilicate glassware containers that serve as both frying baskets and serving dishes. The borosilicate means they can also withstand extreme temperatures, making it easy to take your favourite foods from frozen to crispy, and it's safer to use than any non-stick basket. The Crispi also comes with two removable crisping grates and two snap-on container lids for easy food-storage post-feast.
This compact manual coffee machine can pour up to two espresso shots at once and features a steam wand for cafe-quality milk foaming. There's no built-in grinder, but you either use ground coffee beans or invest in a separate grinder using the cash you save with this deal.
If you've already got a decent coffee maker but one without a grinder, just add this Breville machine to get fresh ground coffee. It has over 60 settings for precise control over your beans, meaning you should be able to extract the most delicious shot from the grind catering to your taste.
A welcome saving on Breville's answer to the SodaStream. Not only can you use the InFizz Fusion to carbonate water, but you can fizz any liquid you can think of — other than hot beverages of course. This nifty machine is sure to be a hit during at-home cocktail nights.
Offering “incredible sound” according to our review, the Bose Ultra Open Earbuds have all the power and quality you’d expect from a Bose-branded item while providing the benefits of an open-ear form factor. The Immersive sound is excellent, and they give up to 7 hours of music. While they have been slightly cheaper, this is the not far off the best price we have seen since lately.
We gave these stunning earbuds 4.5 stars in our review as they have class-leading audio handling and impeccable sound quality that rivals the best wireless earbuds. With balanced sound, effective ANC and a great battery life, these Sennheiser buds will make any audiophile smile.
We've not reviewed this set of Beats earbuds just yet, but we've been impressed with the brand's previous efforts, including the previous Beats Fit Pro. This newer model has a more secure fit, perfect for workout sessions, a smaller case and full IPX4 water and sweat resistance. They don't get the heart-rate sensor as found in the Powerbeats Pro unfortunately, but otherwise this is a cracking set of in-ear headphones.
The Ninja Slushi lets you skip the ice and still enjoy perfectly smooth icy drinks with very little effort. Check out our Ninja Slushi review for the full rundown.
It's got a cult-like following and two members of our own staff are massive fans. If you love your chilled desserts — ice creams, gelatos, smoothies — but want to control your calorie intake, you really should consider getting the Ninja Creami. This Deluxe edition gets you three containers, which is great value at this price.
We haven’t reviewed this Bose soundbar, but if it’s anything like the brand’s other models, we’re confident it will do a mighty fine job of boosting the sound from your TV, ideal when watching movies. If you want to add even more low-end grunt, it works with the company’s Bass Modules (sold separately). A Dialogue mode helps to boost vocals, and if you fancy a dance around your bedroom or living room, Bluetooth is onboard for you to stream your favourite tunes.
While not the lowest price we've seen, this is still a great deal on Apple's flagship earbuds. The ANC is best-in-class, and the sound and fit have been improved over the Pro 2. Check out our review for the full story.
As a recent addition to Samsung's well-received budget tablet range, the A11 picks up where the A9 left off, and at the same price too. This is the base model, with just Wi-Fi connectivity and 128GB of storage, but you can expand that easily to up to 2TB via a microSD card. If you need an Android tablet for daily use like browsing, watching videos and maybe playing a few games, this one's well worth considering, although it has been available for less than AU$300 previously.
Not a big discount and even I balk at recommending a toaster that costs more then AU$50, but I have the Black Truffle model of this 2-slice toaster and trust me when I say it's one of the best toasters I've used. Sure, it's overkill for the average person but if you can get the perfect toast every morning (or arvo or evening), I think it's worth considering.
The Vivoactive 5 contains a lot of the premium Garmin features found in its more expensive offerings, while also priced closer to conventional smartwatches. These features include on-board GPS, on-device storage for offline music via Spotify, and fitness metrics like Body Battery and VO2 Max.
We called this the best smart ring for battery life (rated up to 12 days + a further 150 days with the charging case) while also being a more affordable option than Oura and Samsung at full price. The Gen 2 added a sleep apnoea tracker to make up for the price hike over its predecessor. Again, be sure to source the sizing kit first as not all smart rings are made the same.
Promising simplicity of use, the De'Longhi Magnifica S has an easy-to-use touch control panel that allows you to brew two cups simultaneously with the minimum amount of effort. It also has a silent integrated grinder with 13 settings, plus a handy milk frother too, so it’s a good all-in-one solution.
The Breville Bambino Plus is incredibly simple to use, and can take care of most of the coffee making process for you. Grind some beans into the porta filter, insert it into the group head and use the one-touch controls to brew. It also has a hands-free milk texturing system for expertly frothed milk, while ThermoJet technology means the machine is ready to use in seconds. There's very little you need to do to simply enjoy the results — now AU$20 more than what it cost at the start of the sale.
It's a pity only one colourway is going for this price, but if you don't mind the dusty pink of Sony's latest flagship cans, you'll be in for a treat. Arguably one of the best headphones available today, there's no doubting performance here, with beautifully balanced sound and great ANC.
With a nice saving, it's hard to dismiss this Breville coffee machine deal. The Barista Express has a built-in grinder, tamper, and bean hopper, so there's no need to buy a separate grinder or hand tamp. Available in a few colourways under the same listing, only the Charcoal model gets the full discount.
If you’re after a coffee that makes itself, then it’s hard to go past the Breville Creatista Plus. A great compact pod machine that uses the Original Nespresso pods, and one that can also do milk frothing without requiring a whole other appliance.
This is a fantastic discount on Dyson's most powerful cordless vacuum to date, and what I like even more about it is the quick-release floorhead so you don't have to keep bending to take off or clip it back in again. For your money, you're getting 315AW of suction and a very powerful motor, a new compression dust cup that can hold up to 30 days of compacted dirt, the new anti-tangle FluffyCones floorhead with dust-illuminating light and long runtime too. If you want the latest from the popular brand, this one is it.
This handheld gaming PC has been cheaper before, dropping to the AU$899 mark but, then again, nothing really comes cheap these days. Importantly, though, this is a great performer, with a vivid 8-inch display and 144Hz refresh rate for smooth gameplay. It's also rather nice looking and comfortable in the hand.
We've only reviewed the more expensive Touch model, but if you take your coffee seriously – and want a barista-level cup of joe easily, this is the deal for you. Offering automatic grinding, dosing, tamping and milk texturing, this machine lets you go from beans to latte in seconds.

articles.title: Italy Fines Meta €805 Million Over Facebook's Android Gallery Access Without Explicit Consent
articles.text:
Meta was fined €805 million in Italy yesterday over a Facebook for Android feature that suggests photos and videos from users' phone galleries for them to post.
The Garante, Italy's data protection authority, found that the feature was enabled by default and that the app accessed Italian users' photos, videos, and related metadata without their explicit consent.
The company has 60 days to switch the feature off by default, including for people who have already granted the app gallery access, and to request consent separately.
Meta plans to appeal and calls the fine "disproportionate", a spokesperson said in a statement reported by Reuters.
The app asks for gallery access via a single permission that covers the whole app and several functions with different purposes, the authority found. A general notice about enabling other features appears first, but it does not make it clear to users that they are also enabling gallery suggestions.
Fully granted, a permission like this lets the app read the phone's whole photo archive, usually on an ongoing basis. Neither the user nor the authority can check which information is actually used.
The authority found a breach of Article 122 of Italy's Privacy Code, which puts the EU's ePrivacy Directive into Italian law. That rule treats a phone as part of a person's private life. Any access to what the phone stores, therefore, requires free and informed consent, whether or not data is sent anywhere or harm results.
The authority's order, set out in its press release, requires the company to:
- Within 60 days, ask for consent through a separate, specific request for this feature, and explain clearly what the feature is for, that it accesses the gallery, and how to turn it off.
- Within 60 days, keep the feature off by default, including for people who already granted the permission.
- Within 30 days, report to the authority on the work it has started, and within 90 days, on the measures it has taken.
If the company misses the 60-day deadline, the feature cannot be switched on for anyone who has not given valid consent.
Meta said in a statement quoted in a Reuters report that the feature works only after users give permission on their device, and that they can change that permission at any time in their settings.
The Centro Tutela Consumatori Utenti, the Bolzano consumer protection group whose complaint started the investigation, published consumer advice on July 11, 2025. It told users to switch off the gallery suggestion settings in the app and to check what access and permissions the Facebook app has on their phone.
The investigation did not look at whether gallery content was used to train AI models. The company denies any such use. The authority may separately examine a newer feature, launched this year, that allows gallery content to be processed in the cloud.
The company had argued that Ireland's data protection authority should handle the case. The Garante rejected that argument because the ePrivacy rules do not provide a one-stop-shop mechanism.
The feature has been available since 2023. The investigation began in July 2025 and included the authority's own technical analysis.
The fine equals about 0.47% of the group's global revenue. In setting it, the authority weighed the large number of people involved, about 20 million Android users in Italy.
It also weighed how long the breach has lasted. The breach is still ongoing for people who have not updated the app, and for those who have already granted permission, the authority said.
Other factors were a 2019 decision against the company and limited cooperation during the investigation. Changes the company made after the complaint counted in its favor, though the authority judged them late and limited to people who update the app.

articles.title: De 480p a la distorsión: el polémico reescalado con supuesta IA que alteró el rostro de Gustavo Cerati
articles.text:
Lisa y Benito Cerati, hijos del músico Gustavo Cerati, dijeron que no fueron consultados sobre el tratamiento que recibió el videoclip de ‘Me quedo aquí’, publicado para celebrar los 20 años del disco ‘Ahí vamos’. Seguidores del cantante sospechan que se usó inteligencia artificial para modificar su rostro.
Los hermanos, ambos músicos, difundieron un mensaje en las historias de Instagram de Lisa, que Benito volvió a publicar. Primero elogiaron la remasterización del audio del álbum: dijeron que sentían que “hacía falta” y que respeta el deseo original de un sonido más crudo.
Sobre el video, en cambio, fueron críticos. “Me quedo aquí recibió un tratamiento que nosotros no vimos antes que todos ustedes y nos pareció desfavorable”, escribieron. Agregaron que no estaban al tanto del proceso de mejora ni de las herramientas empleadas: “No fuimos consultados y lamentamos mucho eso”.
La polémica comenzó el 10 de noviembre, cuando la cuenta oficial de Gustavo Cerati en X compartió un fragmento del clip. El mensaje decía que, además de la edición remasterizada del disco y del video en alta definición de Crimen, “se trabajó en la mejora” del videoclip de ‘Me quedo aquí’.
Fans que no reconocen el rostro del cantante
Las críticas se concentraron en el aspecto de Cerati. Según el sitio Indie Hoy, varios usuarios cuestionaron los cambios en sus rasgos y gestos. Uno de los comentarios más votados habló de “un reescalado con IA que lo hizo ver todo super artificial”. Otro lo describió como una versión que “traiciona lo original”.
El portal Tercer Parlante agregó que algunos seguidores notaron una imagen poco sincronizada con la voz y una mirada distorsionada. Otros consideraron innecesario explotar la imagen de un artista que murió en 2014, a los 55 años, y dijeron que preferirían material inédito.
Ni la cuenta oficial ni los hijos del músico confirmaron que se haya utilizado inteligencia artificial. El mensaje original solo habla de una “mejora” del video, que circulaba en una resolución de 480p. Los medios consultados no encontraron un detalle público de las herramientas empleadas.
El caso de ‘Crimen’, el primer sencillo del álbum, tuvo otra recepción. Según el medio argentino Piloto de Tormenta, el clip fue filmado en 2006 por Joaquín Cambre con una cámara de alta definición, de modo que bastó recuperar el material original. Los comentarios sobre ese adelanto fueron positivos, informó Tercer Parlante.
El audio también se trató de otra manera. De acuerdo con esos medios, el ingeniero Adam Ayan remasterizó el disco con la supervisión de Tweety González, coproductor del álbum, y de Héctor Castillo. Se mantuvieron las mezclas originales y se ganó claridad en los agudos y en el rango dinámico.
Un debate que ya existía con Soda Stereo
La discusión sobre el uso de tecnología con la imagen de Cerati tiene un antecedente. Soda Stereo, la banda que el cantante integró, anunció una gira continental llamada ‘Ecos’ con una versión digital de él en pantalla, según recordó Indie Hoy.
Para esos recitales se creó un modelo tridimensional a partir de miles de horas de archivo, sobre todo de la gira ‘Me Verás Volver’, de 2007. Los técnicos combinaron inteligencia artificial, renderizado 3D y captura de movimiento. El resultado, indicó el mismo medio, tuvo tanto defensores como detractores.
‘Ahí vamos’ salió el 4 de abril de 2006 y fue el cuarto álbum de estudio de Cerati como solista. ‘Crimen’ ganó el Latin Grammy a la mejor canción de rock ese año, según Tercer Parlante. La edición remasterizada llegó a las plataformas digitales el 12 de noviembre y a los formatos físicos el 13.
Según los medios consultados, la cuenta oficial de Cerati no respondió públicamente al mensaje de sus hijos, y no hay confirmación de qué técnica se aplicó al videoclip de ‘Me quedo aquí’.

articles.title: Original Mass Effect composer shares how a blind audition got him the job after BioWare ‘gravitated’ toward his demo music — ‘No one knew whose music was attributed to which composer’
articles.text:
Original Mass Effect composer looks back on the audition process for the ‘mystery’ RPG codenamed ‘SFX’ and how he had to ‘earn’ the job through a blind audition — ‘They gravitated to mine and were very happy to find out it was me!’
Sam Hulick was also chosen, and his demo music would later become 'Uncharted Worlds'
- Original Mass Effect composer Jack Wall recalls how he landed the job at BioWare
- Wall says he created demo music for the "mystery" RPG dubbed "SFX," and BioWare chose him after a blind audition
- He says, "They gravitated to mine and were very happy to find out it was me! I love that story because I had to earn it"
Jack Wall, the composer for the original Mass Effect, has shared the story of how he landed the job on BioWare's now-iconic sci-fi role-playing game (RPG).
In an interview with TechRadar Gaming, Wall recalled that he was offered a chance to audition for Mass Effect after working on Jade Empire and "had a pretty good time doing that."
"Of course, then it had a code name: 'SFX'," Wall recalled. "It was a mystery."
The composer explained that he created some demo music, then got a call shortly after from BioWare producer Shauna Perry, who told Wall they did a blind audition of all the entries to single out their favorite.
"No one knew whose music was attributed to which composer," he said. "They gravitated to mine and were very happy to find out it was me! I love that story because I had to earn it."
Wall continued, saying, "I went to BioWare in Edmonton to do our kickoff meeting, and they said there was this one composer, Sam Hulick, who did this one piece that they really liked (the demo that became 'Uncharted Worlds'). I think I said, 'Why did you hire me?' (laughs)."
'Uncharted Worlds' is, of course, one of Mass Effect's most memorable tracks, and Hulick also came on board, too.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
"He was very young in his career at the time, so they were reluctant to hire him outright on his own, but having us both made sense," Wall said. "I honestly love that piece, and Sam killed it."
The Mass Effect and Mass Effect 2 scores were a collaborative effort, featuring Wall, Hulick, Richard Jacques, and David Kates, with Jimmy Hinson lending his talent on the sequel. They're two of the best RPG soundtracks of all time, and according to Wall, the other BioWare developers had their favorite tracks.
Namely, 'Vigil', 'Uncharted Worlds', 'The Normandy', and 'The Citadel', Wall said, adding that game director Casey Hudson called him after he'd completed 'Noveria' and told him, "This was his dream piece fulfilling the brief he had asked for initially."
"From ME2, of course, 'Suicide Mission', 'The Illusive Man' and 'Reflections'," Wall added. "I’m going from memory here, so opinions on the dev team may vary!"
Wall also told TechRadar Gaming that 'Suicide Mission' was one of the first things he and Casey Hudson worked on together and is "Probably to date one of the 10 best endings for a video game ever."
