articles.title: upGrad broadens its business with new workforce advisory venture
articles.text:
upGrad broadens its business with new workforce advisory venture
upGrad launches workforce advisory business as it expands beyond skilling, aiming to help organisations navigate AI-led transformation through integrated workforce strategy and implementation.
Edtech firm upGrad has launched upGrad Next, a workforce advisory business intended to help organisations redesign how they structure, hire, reward and develop employees as artificial intelligence (AI) reshapes work.
The move broadens upGrad’s corporate offering as it diversifies beyond skilling into higher education, professional courses, study-abroad services and enterprise learning. Its acquisition of Unacademy adds competitive exam preparation to its edtech portfolio, as the company, led by chairperson and co-founder Ronnie Screwvala, eyes a potential IPO.
Anandorup Ghose will lead Next as managing director, with Hrishikesh Godbole, Krishna Chaitanya and Dinkar Pawan among the initial team.
Screwvala described the launch as a response to the next phase of digital change. “The last decade, in many ways, was about the complete digital transformation of organisations. We see the next decade being about transforming the workforce to manage, and get strong returns from, the change that has already happened.”
Next will advise on organisational structure, recruitment, pay and workforce development, and help put those decisions into practice. upGrad said it will combine experienced advisers with AI and its skilling and hiring operations, with accountability for outcomes rather than consultant time billed.
Ghose, who has spent more than 24 years in HR and rewards consulting, worked as a partner at Aon and Deloitte and led the latter’s rewards consulting practice globally. He sees a gap between large technology transformation programmes and specialist products. “These demand experience and judgment. The next decade won't be won by those who adopt technology fastest, but by those who unlock human potential most effectively.”
His argument is that decisions about AI investment, job design and employee capability need to be made together. Technology adoption alone does not guarantee higher productivity.
Aon’s 2026 Human Capital Trends study found that 43% of organisations in India had deployed AI and a further 20% were piloting it, but translating investment into workforce outcomes remained difficult. The World Economic Forum’s Future of Jobs Report 2025 estimated that 39% of workers’ existing skill sets would be transformed or become outdated by 2030, while 63% of employers saw skills gaps as a major barrier to business transformation.
Consulting and technology firms are also combining these capabilities. In October 2026, KPMG in India and HR technology company PeopleStrong announced an alliance pairing workforce advice with AI-enabled human capital management software for employee data and HR processes. In September, Deloitte launched an Open Model Engineering practice to help organisations build and deploy AI tools for business use, and said it would hire and train specialists to work alongside clients. Both moves highlight the growing overlap between advice and implementation.
Meanwhile, the Government programmes are expanding the skills pipeline. The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship said the Skill India Digital Hub’s SOAR programme now includes 50 AI and AI-application qualifications. By August 2026, more than 517,000 learners had enrolled and over 100,000 had been certified.

articles.title: Intel lance le Core Ultra 7 260K : un processeur « exclusif » que vous ne trouverez pas de sitôt
articles.text:
Drôle d'idée que ce processeur en architecture Arrow Lake, mais réservé à un unique revendeur de matériel informatique, Newegg.
Mais quelle mouche a donc piqué les responsables marketing de chez Intel ? Si le groupe américain lance un nouveau processeur baptisé Core Ultra 260K, il ne souhaite visiblement pas que tout le monde puisse en profiter et confirme qu'il sera en « disponibilité limitée ».
BenQ iScreenBar : la barre lumineuse qui s’accorde avec l’iMac
Des lignes en harmonie avec celles de l’ordinateur d’Apple, une conception rigoureuse, des matériaux sélectionnés, rien n’a été laissé au hasard, tout comme le service qu’elle rend une fois allumée !
Baroud d'honneur pour Arrow Lake ?
Il y a déjà deux ans de cela – le 5 novembre 2024 pour être précis –, Intel lançait ses premiers processeurs basés sur l'architecture Arrow Lake et introduisait alors du même coup un nouveau socket, le LGA-1851.
De l'eau a coulé sous les ponts depuis ce lancement des Core Ultra 9 285K, Core Ultra 7 265K et Core Ultra 5 245K. D'autres puces ont, bien sûr, été commercialisées pour enrichir l'offre d'Intel avec, par exemple, les Core Ultra 5 235 et Core Ultra 5 225F en novembre 2025 et les Core Ultra 5 250K Plus et Core Ultra 7 270K Plus en mars de cette année.
Ces derniers ont d'ailleurs été l'occasion d'une sorte de « refresh » de la gamme avec pas mal de très bons points comme une optimisation énergétique notable et un positionnement tarifaire très intéressant. Reste que la gamme Arrow Lake est moins riche que de coutume chez Intel et, à vrai dire, ce n'est pas la nouvelle puce du jour qui va vraiment changer la donne.
Intel commercialise effectivement depuis quelques jours un Core Ultra 7 260K que la firme n'avait jamais présenté. C'est donc une « sortie surprise » pour une puce techniquement très proche du Core Ultra 7 265K.
Un CPU pour l'heure exclusif au revendeur Newegg
Reposant bien évidemment sur le socket LGA-1851, ce Core Ultra 7 260K est doté de 20 cœurs, organisés en 8 cœurs performants (P-core) et 12 cœurs efficaces (E-core).
Le cache de troisième niveau est de 30 Mo, le TDP est donné pour 125 W et la prise en charge de la mémoire vive est limitée à 256 Go de DDR5-6400. Autant de caractéristiques strictement identiques à celles du Core Ultra 7 265K. En réalité, pour trouver des différences entre les deux processeurs, il faut se tourner vers les fréquences de fonctionnement.
Et encore, les fréquences de base sont identiques (3,9 GHz pour les P-core et 3,3 GHz pour les E-core), ce sont les fréquences boost qui sont – légèrement – revues à la baisse : on perd ainsi 100 MHz seulement pour les P-core (5,3 GHz contre 5,4 GHz) comme pour les E-core (4,5 GHz contre 4,6 GHz). On peut raisonnablement se poser la question de l'intérêt d'un tel CPU ?
On comprend (un peu) mieux l'objectif quand on ajoute une précision : le Core Ultra 7 260K ne sera disponible qu'en version « tray », c'est-à-dire sans boîte, pour les assembleurs. Plus important encore, comme le précise le site Tom's Hardware, il semble que la disponibilité de cette puce soit très restreinte, on ne parle pour le moment que d'un seul assembleur.
L'Américain Newegg propose effectivement deux configurations conçues autour de cette puce. Il est donc le seul à disposer de ce Core Ultra 7 260K qui, on l'imagine, est proposé un peu moins cher que le Core Ultra 7 265K. À voir, si dans les prochaines semaines, d'autres intégrateurs y ont droit.
Source : Tom's Hardware

articles.title: Microsoft 365 outage leads to chlorine gas poisoning of 15 hotel guests — email warning system fails, 40 first responders deployed for triage, four taken to hospital
articles.text:
Microsoft 365 outage leads to chlorine gas poisoning of 15 hotel guests — email warning system fails, 40 first responders deployed for triage, four taken to hospital
Safety systems depending on a single service could lead to catastrophic results if that service fails.
Fifteen guests at a hotel in Germany suffered from chlorine gas poisoning because of the recent Microsoft cloud services outage. The establishment had a “maintenance safety system” for its sauna area that relied on sending emails to warn the operators if the chlorine level in the area was too high. Unfortunately, the service disruption meant that the system's messages could not be sent, leading to increased levels that precipitated human injuries, writes Notebookcheck. German emergency services had to deploy 40 first responders to the site, with local media reporting that four victims were taken to the hospital for treatment, with one remaining for further observation.
The tech giant experienced a global outage affecting Outlook and other services from November 12 to 14, which led some Japanese workers to dust off their fax machines to keep their business running. Although this Microsoft outage wasn’t as large as the CrowdStrike fiasco in 2024, which led to a massive service disruption to a good number of corporate computer systems and sent shockwaves across the world, this incident has caused injuries and could’ve even led to something more catastrophic if the issue wasn’t caught earlier.
This is one of the issues that institutions must consider when using online services or the Internet of Things to automate systems, especially those that are crucial for safety. Architects of such systems should always have a physical or analog backup that will continue operating even if everything goes offline. More importantly, their people should know that they exist and be familiar with how they work. Alternatively, businesses can host their own servers, build their own automations, and run everything locally, although this would require a bit more involvement in building and programming the entire system. And there could be local infrastructure impacting issues like power cuts, still.
Aside from that, the Microsoft outage also highlights the corporate world’s increasing reliance on a few big tech companies. While tech giants like Microsoft, Google, and AWS have the advantage of economies of scale, allowing them to offer their services reliably and more affordably compared to smaller rivals or an in-house deployment, it also means that if they go down, they affect millions of businesses that rely on them and cause economic activity to grind to a halt.

Jowi Morales is a tech enthusiast with years of experience working in the industry. He’s been writing with several tech publications since 2021, where he’s been interested in tech hardware and consumer electronics.

articles.title: Menos chuletón, más lentejas: un estudio finlandés relaciona la proteína vegetal con niveles más altos de testosterona
articles.text:
El imaginario tradicional relaciona la testosterona con hombres muy viriles y a esos hombres viriles los asocia mucho más con un buen chuletón que con un plato de lentejas. Sin embargo, según un estudio publicado recientemente por científicos finlandeses, el consumo de proteína vegetal se asocia con niveles más altos de testosterona que el de proteína animal. Habrá personas a las que esto les sorprenda muchísimo, pero vamos a ver los datos.
Más de 2.000 participantes. Los datos para llevar a cabo este estudio se tomaron en Finlandia, entre 1984 y 1989. En total, participaron 2.546 hombres, con edades comprendidas entre los 42 y los 60 años. A todos ellos se les hizo registrar su alimentación durante cuatro días y se les tomaron muestras de sangre para analizar tanto los niveles de testosterona como los de SHBG. Esta última es una proteína que se une a la testosterona en sangre para regular la cantidad que está biológicamente activa.
Cabe destacar que los participantes no eran vegetarianos o carnívoros. Todos ellos seguían una alimentación omnívora, pero con diferencias en el consumo de cada tipo de proteína.
Los resultados. Al analizar toda esa información, se vio que los hombres que consumían más proteína animal tenían de media 1,2 nmol/l menos de testosterona total que los de menor consumo. Por otro lado, los que consumían más proteína vegetal tenían 1,1 nmol/l más que los del grupo con menor consumo. Más específicamente, la proteína procedente de lácteos se asoció con menos testosterona total y menos SHBG, mientras que la proteína de carne se asoció con menos SHBG, pero no afectó a la testosterona total. En cuanto a la proteína vegetal de verduras y otras fuentes distintas de los cereales, se vinculó con más testosterona total.
Limitaciones. Las diferencias en los niveles de testosterona y SHBG son estadísticamente significativas, pero no muy grandes. Por eso, no podemos saber si, más allá de los resultados analíticos, habría diferencias a nivel de salud. Tampoco se puede saber si los niveles de testosterona se deben a otros hábitos. No se hizo un seguimiento de una misma persona durante varios años ni con un cambio de alimentación, por lo que no se puede establecer bien la causalidad de todo esto.
En resumen. Los resultados de este estudio son curiosos e invitan a seguir investigando en la misma línea. Es innegable que resultan llamativos por lo que vimos al principio de este artículo. Pero ni siquiera sabemos si realmente son relevantes. Lo que sí está más que demostrado es que una dieta basada en plantas, siempre que no esté compuesta por ultraprocesados, supone muchos beneficios para la salud y, a su vez, se relaciona con un descenso de la huella de carbono. No se emite la misma cantidad de gases de efecto invernadero cultivando legumbres que criando cerdos. Quizás la testosterona no sea el mejor argumento para aumentar el consumo de proteínas vegetales, pero nuestra salud y la de nuestro planeta sí lo son.

articles.title: Netflix estrenará en 2027 la serie de Magic: The Gathering tras varios cambios de fecha
articles.text:
Netflix estrenará Planeswalker en 2027, la serie animada basada en el juego de cartas Magic: The Gathering, y publicó la primera imagen oficial. La plataforma anunció el proyecto por primera vez en 2019 y lo reinició después de que sus primeros responsables lo abandonaran.
La serie se hace junto con Hasbro Entertainment y Wizards of the Coast, la empresa que publica el juego. El showrunner (responsable creativo de la producción) es Terry Matalas, conocido por Star Trek: Picard. Cindy Appel es la cocreadora y Patrick Osborne, ganador de un Oscar, es director supervisor y productor ejecutivo.
El estudio de animación es Digic. Según la sinopsis de Wizards of the Coast, la historia se centra en Chandra, una hechicera del fuego perseguida por sus poderes y marcada por su pasado. Ella y otros planeswalkers, como se llama a los magos del juego, deben evitar una guerra que amenaza a miles de mundos.
La ficha de Wizards of the Coast habla de alianzas traicioneras y de conflictos internos de los personajes, y presenta la serie como una saga de fantasía épica sobre el choque entre magos poderosos. Chandra enfrenta además una fuerza descrita como insidiosa.
Matalas y Appel trabajaron juntos en Star Trek: Picard y en VisionQuest, según Netflix. En 2024, Deadline informó que Matalas había sido nombrado responsable de la serie de Marvel sobre Visión para Disney+. Mientras que Osborne ganó el Oscar por el cortometraje animado Feast.
Siete años de cambios en el proyecto
Netflix anunció en 2019 una serie de Magic con los hermanos Joe y Anthony Russo como productores ejecutivos, según Deadline. Henry Gilroy y Jose Molina serían los guionistas principales. Los Russo y su equipo se fueron por diferencias creativas sobre cómo adaptar la propiedad, y en agosto de 2021 asumió Jeff Kline.
Kline también dejó el proyecto. En septiembre de 2024, Netflix lo relanzó con Matalas al frente, durante su evento Geeked Week. Brandon Routh, que iba a poner la voz de Gideon Jura, dijo entonces que la serie estaba cancelada. Deadline aclaró que solo se descartó la versión anterior, con Routh fuera del nuevo equipo.
Netflix describe la serie como una adaptación nueva del juego. “Tenemos la posibilidad de dar vida a estos personajes de formas que el público no ha visto”, dijo Matalas a la plataforma.
Un juego con 150 países y más de USD 1.000 millones al año
Magic: The Gathering fue creado en 1993 por Richard Garfield y lo publica Wizards of the Coast, una filial de Hasbro. Según Hasbro, citada por Deadline, el juego reúne a decenas de millones de jugadores de mesa y digitales en más de 150 países, con ingresos anuales superiores a USD 1.000 millones.
La marca tendrá además una película con actores, según Deadline. La producen Legendary Entertainment y Hasbro, y Maya Hawke figura como protagonista, según el medio, que lo publicó en exclusiva.
Netflix y Wizards of the Coast confirmaron que Planeswalker se estrenará en 2027, sin precisar mes ni día.
Cómo ver películas en Netflix sin internet
Netflix permite ver películas y series sin internet gracias a su función de descargas, disponible en Android, iPhone, iPad, Fire y Chromebook.
Para usarla, conviene tener la aplicación actualizada y espacio suficiente, ya que el contenido se guarda solo en el dispositivo donde se descargó.
El acceso está en la pestaña “Mi Netflix”, en “Descargas”. Allí se elige el título y se presiona el botón con flecha hacia abajo, preferentemente conectado a WiFi.
Las series admiten descargar episodios sueltos o temporadas completas, con un máximo de 100 descargas activas por dispositivo.
Para reproducir sin conexión, se vuelve a “Mi Netflix” y se selecciona “Reproducir”. Los títulos tienen vigencia limitada y se eliminan si se cancela la suscripción.

articles.title: Intel Razor Lake Gets a 12 P-Core bLLC Chip With No E-Cores, Per Leak
articles.text:
Sunday, November 15th 2026
Intel Razor Lake Gets a 12 P-Core bLLC Chip With No E-Cores, Per Leak
Intel's Razor Lake desktop lineup could include an unlocked gaming chip with 12 P-cores and no regular E-cores at all. Well-known Intel leaker Jaykihn shared the "12+0+4" configuration on X, which pairs those 12 P-cores with four low-power E-cores and Intel's big Last Level Cache (bLLC), the company's answer to AMD's X3D chips. In a follow-up post, he said this SKU replaces a locked 8+0+4 bLLC part that was rumored earlier. Apparently, all 12 P-cores sit on a single compute die designed only for P-cores, rather than a hybrid die with its E-cores switched off, and Jaykihn later said that tile is built on Intel's own 18A-P node. That would make it an outlier, since most Razor Lake compute tiles are reportedly headed to TSMC.
Jaykihn also claims the 125 W 6+12+4 bLLC chip, one of the two 22-core Nova Lake-S parts that leaked back in July, has been pushed from Nova Lake to Razor Lake. If that's accurate, it seems Nova Lake-S will launch with one less bLLC option than expected. There's no word on the 65 W version. Razor Lake-S is currently a 2028 product that should use the same LGA-1954 socket as Nova Lake-S, according to Jaykihn's earlier posts. Intel has listed Razor Lake model IDs in its ISA reference, but none of these specs are official. Plans this far out can change, so it's reasonable to treat the 12 P-core chip as just a target for now.
Sources:
				Jaykihn on X 1, 				2, 				3, 				via Videocardz

There will be clock speed limits no matter what due to the number of P-cores unless Intel is making large changes to their boosting algorithms which will effect the vast majority of usage. It won't be as fast as NVL bLLC parts though it should be close, but it should be well short of RZL bLLC parts. It should appeal to buyers who complain about E-cores though because they'll think they're getting something better.

articles.title: With Starship catch, SpaceX still shows it can dazzle the world
articles.text:
STARBASE, Texas—The black and silver ship fell out of the sky, emerging from the cloud deck near the very end of its flight. Incongruously, the rocket flew horizontal until the last moment when three Raptor rocket engines ignited and it swooped into a vertical position.
Slowly, gently, haltingly, the Starship upper stage eased its way toward the waiting tower where two arms extended outward, awaiting expectantly. The margins are so incredibly narrow. Two nubs on either side of the rocket, each protruding only about one foot, were the only purchase the rocket would have on the arms.
Then, less than a minute after it came into view, the Starship upper stage was snagged by the launch tower, as snug as you like. And so it was all over. SpaceX, nearly a quarter of a century after its founding, had just taken a hugely significant step toward developing and optimizing a massive, rapidly reusable rocket.
We are dazzled
This was a breathtaking feat; a brilliant technical achievement that required the best engineering minds to think through a million different, difficult problems. And on Saturday evening, following a handful of practice runs into the Indian Ocean, they did it before the entire world.
Watching Starship launch from here a little less than a day earlier, and knowing it had orbited the planet multiple times, added to the sense of unreality in seeing this spaceship return to Earth under its own power, and be captured by the tower.
It felt like stepping into the future. SpaceX has dazzled us before, by landing rockets on barges and returning humans to space with Crew Dragon. But this flight took things to another level. Starships are huge. They carry a huge amount of energy coming back from orbit. And until a few years ago, it seemed beyond fantastical to think about capturing a rocket with what are essentially outsized chopsticks.
Nevertheless, it happened.
Rapid reuse is firmly on the horizon
Humans have built reusable spacecraft that flew into orbit before. In the 1970s, flush with confidence after the triumphant Moon landings, NASA designed and built several Space Shuttles. They had solid rocket boosters that were fished from the ocean and reused. The large orange external tank was not recovered after each flight, but the orbiters went to space for two weeks, or even longer, before returning to Earth and landing on a runway.

articles.title: Flaming Hydra’s new Kickstarter campaign rethinks e-book ownership and digital lending | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Here’s a big promise: A new Kickstarter campaign aims to usher in the “return of the human internet.”
That’s the tagline of a crowdfunding campaign for The Phoenix Project, an initiative from the online culture and commentary magazine Flaming Hydra. If you back The Phoenix Project, you’re supporting three things — a one-off print magazine designed to celebrate “the values and fun of the early internet,” a new e-book service for libraries, and a newsletter subscription/archiving program that’s also designed for libraries.
To Flaming Hydra’s lead editor Maria Bustillos, these disparate projects are “basically all one thing,” tied together by the goal of “protecting freedom of information” and fulfilling the “promise of the early internet, where you’re making information available to as many people as possible, while still protecting the right of artists and authors to make a living.”
Bustillos told me that these issues have been highlighted on Flaming Hydra itself, for example when Tal Levin wrote about finding countless AI-generated clones of his book on Amazon. By “creating an ecosystem that is based in people working together, who are offering their stuff in a context that is controlled and doesn’t allow” others to create and sell AI-generated clones, Bustillos said Flaming Hydra is “part of the human project.”
“AI is not this unstoppable force,” she added. “If people just set up publishing pipelines and networks and organizations that are dedicated to the human internet, people who want to read stuff can go to them, and it’s actually completely isolated from mechanistic interference.”
The Phoenix Project fits into this vision by making the work of human writers more accessible to libraries.
Back in 2020, Bustillos wrote about the e-book systems dominating libraries and schools. In one example, instead of just buying a book, a school had to pay $27 per student per year for continued access to copies of “The Diary of Anne Frank.”
This is symptomatic of a broader system that treats true ownership of e-books and other digital media as a thing of the past. Instead, we “license” these e-books from their publishers, and they can be altered or removed at any time.
“E-books are books,” Bustillos said. “They’re not some other thing. They are books, and people should be able to own them, and libraries should be able to own them, and media should be able to be owned. All digital media should be able to be owned.”
In her view, ownership boils down to a simple question: “If you are at the mercy of somebody who can shut the book off, you do not own it.”
So even beyond the question of ongoing payments, there have also been examples of e-books being altered or removed from readers’ devices long after their purchase. Bustillos acknowledged that for individual pieces of media, this distinction may not seem like a big deal, “but if it’s all the textbooks for everybody, if it’s all the books,” then it’s a real problem.
Flaming Hydra and The Phoenix Project seek to solve this by letting libraries truly purchase and own e-books. They can then lend those e-books to their patrons through a new, open source “library in a box” system called Lenny for Libraries.
The Phoenix Project is starting by offering five new e-books from Flaming Hydra writers, including collections of writing from The Awl, and of essays by Tom Scocca and Bustillos herself. That might sound like a relatively small start, but Bustillos said she’s talking to library consortiums and author groups, and the goal here is to “change the conversation” around e-books and digital archiving and lending. So The Phoenix Project could be paving the way for other initiatives that follow a similar model.
Similarly, The Phoenix Foundry Archive is designed to make paywalled newsletter content available to libraries. Bustillos noted that “so much of the best journalism, criticism, essays” is now being published in paywalled newsletters that are inaccessible to libraries (as well as the Internet Archive).
With Phoenix, newsletter writers (starting with those who use Ghost, with support for additional newsletter platforms coming in the future) will be able to offer subscriptions to libraries, similar to the way libraries can subscribe to newspapers and magazines. Once it’s set up, Phoenix will automatically convert whichever newsletter posts the writer wants into EPUB documents, which are then sent to libraries for digital lending.
Flaming Hydra has been working on all this even before launching the Kickstarter, and Bustillos said she was grateful for the financial support from backers like Anand Raganathan, Brewster Kahle, and Paul Ford. But by turning to crowdfunding, Bustillos said Flaming Hydra can better protect the work, ensuring that it remains sustainable and independent.
“We don’t have to be at the mercy of anybody, and it also protects editorial independence,” she said. “Those things go hand in hand.”
Flaming Hydra seeks to raise $30,000 for The Phoenix Project, with the campaign ending on November 27.

articles.title: ‘Harder than Dark Souls’: this might just be the toughest gaming boss of 2026 — here’s how I emerged victorious against this brutal opponent in Nintendo Switch Sports Resort
articles.text:
Dark Souls is nothing compared to this: I wasn’t expecting a Mii to push me to my limits in Nintendo Switch Sports Resort, but this one boss battle had me absolutely raging
I see this Mii in my nightmares
Here’s a question: what titles spring to mind when you think about hard video games? You might consider 2025’s Hollow Knight: Silksong, perhaps a classic like Battletoads — and Dark Souls would certainly pop up in my head.
But what if I told you that this seemingly cuddly-by-comparison Nintendo Switch 2 game has challenged me more than anything else I’ve played this year?
Yes, I just faced off against a boss in the Island Crown mode of Nintendo Switch Sports Resort that pushed me to my very limit. No, really, this was harder than Dark Souls. “Who is this opponent that you speak of?” I hear you cry. Well, it’s none other than the Wii Sports Resort table tennis aficionado, Lucía.
Here’s the deal. In Island Crown (a predominantly single-player mode), you have to climb a ranking table for each respective sport, in a bid to topple the Island Champion and reign supreme. But after you finally rank #1, it turns out that your journey is far from over.
See, reaching the top rank unlocks a unique showdown against a Legend — a highly skilled Mii from Wii Sports Resort and related titles. These Legend matches range from fair yet challenging to absolutely rage-inducing. And for me, the table tennis game against Lucía was the worst of the worst.
Everything about her — whether that be her movement speed, her pinpoint precision, her unshakeable resolve in the face of power shots — made her an extremely formidable opponent. I may have played through titles like Bloodborne and Shin Megami Tensei III: Nocturne before, but their challenge levels pale in comparison to this.
Across my (extremely) numerous attempts, Lucía seemed to return even the most challenging shots and place the ball in spots that my character could only dream of reaching. After a few 6-0 drubbings, I managed to start picking up some points, playing out long rallies until she made the smallest of errors. But it still wasn’t happening.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
An hour or so in, though, and I felt like I was getting somewhere. I’d managed to scrape my way to a few deuces here and there, and with the power of slice shots, I was able to recover to the center of the table and avoid leaving myself exposed.
But it still wasn’t enough. Until one fateful match.
Picture this. The clock strikes midnight. I sit there, Joy-Cons in hand, with dozens of failed attempts to my name. After landing a killer shot, I draw the game level at 4-4. Sweat begins to form on my brow, as my hands tremble — I can feel the arm ache taking over. But I know I have to see this through.
What ensues is a rally of epic proportions. Returned power-shots, jaw-droppingly accurate placements, last-gasp saves…you name it. But as the rally reaches its climax, I spot a gap on Lucía’s left side; I swiftly strike, and I manage to make it 5-4. I just need one more point.
Lucía launches a barrage of cross-table shots, looping curved balls, and seemingly impossible saves, but then suddenly, she scuffs the ball, leaving her open to a devastating smash. I swing the Joy-Con with bated breath as I watch the ball fling across my screen and…she misses. My hellish ordeal against the table tennis queen was finally over.
With a ridiculous smile on my face, about 50 Ls to my name, and the spoils of war (a golden nameplate item) in hand, I put the controllers down, reflected on my life choice to stay up until 1am playing table tennis with a Mii, and hit the hay.
So, there you have it. Have you had the chance to play Nintendo Switch Sports Resort yet? Have you managed to defeat any of the Legends? Maybe you beat Lucía on the first try, and I’m simply awful at this game — whatever the case, I’d love to hear from you, so make sure to get chatting in the comments.
P.S. It turns out that the table tennis Gauntlet, unlocked after beating Lucía, has an even harder Mii to face off against. But for the sake of my own well-being, I’m going to leave that for a later date…

articles.title: Judge denies motion to dismiss DRAM price-fixing lawsuit against Micron, Samsung, and SK hynix — says chipmakers acted like ‘hawks flying in formation,’ finds evidence of DRAM collusion plausible after 500% price surge
articles.text:
Judge denies motion to dismiss DRAM price-fixing lawsuit against Micron, Samsung, and SK hynix, finds evidence of DRAM collusion plausible after 500% price surge — says chipmakers acted like ‘hawks flying in formation'
This does not mean that the defendants are guilty, though.
Judge Noël Wise, who presides over the proposed class-action lawsuit against Micron, Samsung, and SK hynix, has denied the companies’ motion to have the case dismissed. According to the decision, the defendants’ argument that the legal action is just “a rerun” of the same antitrust case filed against the industry in 2018 was rejected as the plaintiffs have established that there’s some new evidence suggesting that there was collusion between the big three memory chip manufacturers.
Micron, Samsung, and SK hynix argued that they watch each other like hawks because of how tight competition is. Judge Wise disagreed with this characterization, though, saying that what they are accused of goes beyond that. “Their contentions are more akin to hawks flying in formation — an activity that hawks ordinarily do not do.”
The plaintiffs, which are made up of 17 individuals and small businesses, allege that the companies made four parallel moves that restricted DRAM supply and led to the current shortage, which saw prices jump by as much as 500% in one year. One of the events they cited included the “simultaneous DRAM production cuts” from October 2022 to April 2023, which was quickly followed by a “coordinated pivot to HBM.” They also said that the three companies announced the winding down of DDR4 production in a span of three months and have failed to expand the production capacity “despite these extraordinary prices — the single most powerful supply signal the DRAM industry has ever produced.”
Other factors that the suing parties brought to the table include the introduction of stringent customer vetting procedures in response to the shortage, the refusal to sign long-term contracts for DRAM customers, Micron’s decision to shut down Crucial (its consumer memory brand), multiple statements projecting the shortage, as well as their involvement in previous price-fixing scandals.
The big three memory chip makers argued that all of these are logical business moves so that they can maximize their revenue during a period of great demand and that they are “consistent with [their own] independent self-interest.” They also said that they appear to have similar behaviors because they’re in a highly concentrated market, and that they’re all “reacting to the same market pressures,” thus it would make sense for them to have a similar response.
Despite their rebuttals, the judge decided that the case is plausible enough to move forward. This isn’t a judgment, though — both sides would still have to show their evidence and speak their arguments before the court before getting a decision. Because of this, the three companies are given until December 7 to respond to the original complaint with the case management conference, which will determine the administrative matters on the case, set for January 2027.

articles.title: Tempolimit auf der Autobahn: Warum Deutschland weltweit allein dasteht
articles.text:
120 statt Vollgas: So viel CO2 und Sprit würde ein Tempolimit in Deutschland sparen
Auf fast drei Vierteln der deutschen Autobahnen gibt es kein Tempolimit. Das ist weltweit einzigartig. Dabei machen Autobahnen nur knapp 1,5 Prozent des deutschen Straßennetzes aus. Trotzdem ist der Verkehr auf Autobahnen für mehr als 40 Prozent der CO2-Emissionen von Pkw in Deutschland verantwortlich. Gründe sind die intensive Nutzung der Autobahnen sowie die hohen Durchschnittsgeschwindigkeiten.
Als deutsche Politiker 1971 begannen, erstmals ernsthaft über ein Tempolimit auf Autobahnen nachzudenken, hatten andere europäische Länder solche Regelungen längst eingeführt. Der oft bizarre Streit überlebte in den vergangenen 55 Jahren Öl- und Wirtschaftskrisen, Regierungswechsel und Klimaschutzdebatten. Ein Ende ist nicht abzusehen. Zwei neue Studien bringen wieder Schwung in die Debatte.

articles.title: Facebook condamné à 805 millions d’euros en Italie pour accès à des photos sans consentement
articles.text:
Pendant que vous faites défiler votre fil Facebook sur un téléphone Android, Meta vous suggère de publier des photos et des vidéos tirées de votre galerie, y compris celles que vous n’avez jamais partagées. En Italie, cette fonction n'a pas plu à l’autorité de protection des données, qui a infligé à Meta une amende de 805 millions d’euros.
Comme l’explique le Garante, l’autorité italienne de protection des données, Meta a eu « accès à des photos, à des vidéos et à leurs métadonnées conservées dans les smartphones des utilisateurs italiens, sans avoir obtenu de consentement spécifique et sans les avoir correctement informés ». Le Garante estime à environ 20 millions le nombre de possesseurs d’un téléphone Android touchés en Italie, et c’est la plus lourde amende de son histoire. Si vous utilisez Facebook sur Android en France, cette fonction de suggestions existe aussi dans votre application.
Meta demandait l’accès à votre galerie avec une seule autorisation
Depuis 2023, Meta glisse dans votre fil des photos et des vidéos de votre téléphone, en guise d’idées de publication. En juillet 2025, le Centre de protection des consommateurs de Bolzano, dans le nord de l’Italie, avait alerté le Garante sur ces suggestions tirées de fichiers jamais publiés.
L’autorité a découvert que Meta demandait une seule autorisation pour lire votre galerie, valable pour toute l’application et pour plusieurs fonctions à la fois. Un message général vous proposait d’activer d’autres fonctionnalités, sans préciser que vos photos serviraient aussi à ces suggestions. Et Meta activait la fonction par défaut.
Le Garante a sanctionné Meta en vertu de la directive européenne ePrivacy, transposée en Italie à l’article 122 du code de la vie privée. Selon l’autorité, votre smartphone fait partie de votre sphère privée, et Meta devait obtenir votre accord avant de lire votre galerie, même sans copier vos fichiers sur ses serveurs ni vous causer de préjudice. D’ici soixante jours, Meta devra vous demander un accord séparé pour ces suggestions, vous expliquer à quoi elles servent et laisser la fonction désactivée par défaut, y compris si vous aviez accepté l’accès à votre galerie.
Vous pouvez couper cet accès sans attendre. Dans les réglages de votre téléphone, ouvrez Applications, puis Facebook, Autorisations et Photos et vidéos, et choisissez « Ne pas autoriser », ou un accès limité aux seuls fichiers que vous sélectionnez si votre version d’Android le propose. Dans Facebook, rendez-vous ensuite dans Paramètres et confidentialité, puis Paramètres, et désactivez les deux options de la rubrique consacrée aux suggestions de partage de la pellicule. La seconde concerne le traitement de vos photos dans le cloud de Meta, une fonction que le Garante examinera à part. L’autorité n’a pas enquêté sur un éventuel entraînement de l’IA de Meta avec vos photos, que l’entreprise dément.
La CNIL peut sanctionner Meta sans passer par l’Irlande
Meta contestait la compétence du Garante et voulait confier le dossier à l’autorité irlandaise, puisque sa filiale européenne est installée à Dublin. Le Garante a rejeté cet argument, car la directive ePrivacy ne prévoit pas de guichet unique, ce mécanisme du RGPD qui réserve la plupart des enquêtes à l’autorité du pays où une entreprise a son siège européen.
En France, la directive est transposée à l’article 82 de la loi Informatique et Libertés, qui encadre aussi la lecture d’informations stockées sur votre appareil. C’est sur ce fondement que la CNIL a infligé à la filiale irlandaise de Shein une amende de 150 millions d’euros pour des cookies déposés sans consentement, sans consulter l’autorité irlandaise. Aucune procédure de la CNIL contre les suggestions de Facebook n’a été rendue publique à ce jour.
« Nous sommes en net désaccord avec l’appréciation des faits et l’application de la loi par le Garante, et nous estimons le montant de la sanction disproportionné », souligne Meta, qui prépare un recours. L’entreprise a aussi annoncé faire appel de sa condamnation à 25 milliards de dollars au Nouveau-Mexique, où la justice lui reproche d’avoir trompé les utilisateurs de Facebook sur la protection de leurs données.

articles.title: How flexible workspaces are changing the way companies think about offices
articles.text:
How flexible workspaces are changing the way companies think about offices
At TechSparks 2026, Manish Khedia of The Executive Centre discussed how businesses are moving beyond traditional office layouts and long-term leases to focus on flexibility, collaboration, and employee needs.
The COVID-19 pandemic changed how companies think about offices. After employees spent months working from home, businesses had to reconsider what would bring people back to the workplace and how to make that time productive.
At TechSparks 2026, Manish Khedia, Regional Managing Director at The Executive Centre (TEC), joined Shivani Muthanna, Senior Director – Strategic Content & Video at YourStory, for a fireside chat titled ‘The enterprise office 2.0: Space, strategy, experience redefined’.
The discussion covered how flexible workspaces, hybrid working arrangements, and employee expectations are changing the way businesses plan their offices.
From square footage to collaboration
For years, companies made office decisions based largely on location, square footage, the number of workstations, and the type of building. The pandemic changed those priorities, first by forcing employees to work from home and then by making companies reconsider how to bring them back.
According to Khedia, the challenge now is to create offices that employees want to visit, where they can work productively, collaborate, and have access to the facilities they need.
“I think all the companies are looking at how they can engage their employees to be more productive, not by giving them more work, but by creating an environment where they can collaborate,” he said.
As a result, businesses are looking beyond a premium address when choosing office space. They are considering the surrounding infrastructure, including technology parks, food courts, daycare facilities, and other amenities that make daily work more convenient.
Inside the office, the focus is shifting towards collaboration and employee experience. Companies are moving away from traditional hierarchical layouts toward spaces where people can exchange ideas, work , and think differently.
Khedia said businesses are increasingly treating offices as communities that support employees, rather than simply as fixed assets or status symbols.
Bringing offices closer to employees
Location remains important, particularly in large cities such as Bengaluru and Mumbai, where employees may spend two to three hours commuting each day. The time, cost, and effort involved are among the reasons companies are exploring hybrid working arrangements and the hub-and-spoke model.
Instead of operating from one central office, businesses can set up workspaces in different locations, allowing employees to work closer to home.
Khedia said the aim is to make time spent in the office more productive while reducing the burden of commuting. Employees have more time for themselves, while companies can provide spaces where teams can collaborate.
The shift is not limited to metropolitan cities. Khedia pointed to Ahmedabad, Kochi, and Coimbatore as emerging business hubs, supported by growing talent pools and improving infrastructure.
India’s expanding Global Capability Centre (GCC) ecosystem is also influencing office requirements. Companies are considering not only where talent is available but also whether a location has the infrastructure employees need to work effectively.
Khedia highlighted the quality of India’s commercial real estate developments and the amenities available in premium office buildings across the country.
For companies expanding into new markets, the growing network of business locations provides more options to access talent without requiring employees to relocate to major cities.
Why companies are choosing flexible offices
Business uncertainty is also changing how companies plan their real estate requirements.
Traditional office leases often require companies to commit to space for five to 10 years, based on projections of future growth. But as businesses become more agile, such long-term commitments can be difficult to make.
“If any multinationals come to India, they would first have to invest in real estate, thinking of a five-year horizon. Now, flexible office spaces have cut down on those uncertainties. They have ensured the companies can think for the next one or two years,” Khedia said.
Flexible workspaces allow businesses to start with smaller offices, expand, or reduce their space as required, and pay for what they use. This can help them manage real estate costs and allocate more resources to hiring and other business priorities.
Office design is changing as well. Traditional cabins and cubicles are making way for more open layouts that encourage interaction between teams. Companies are also incorporating greenery and biophilic design to make workplaces more comfortable and inviting.
Flexible workspace providers and landlords
Khedia said flexible workspace providers are increasingly working with traditional landlords rather than competing with them. Such partnerships can help property owners attract more tenants by offering businesses different ways to occupy office space.
“The flex office space is a true partner to the landlord. They're not changing the landscape, they're complementing the landlord to create a space which will invite more and more tenants to that building,” he said.
He pointed to the growth of the sector in India. When he began his career, flexible offices accounted for about 1% of overall real estate leasing. By the last financial quarter, that share had reached 23%, he said.
He also noted that flexible workspace absorption in India had increased from around half a million square feet to more than 17–18 million square feet.
Providers such as TEC now offer more than desks and meeting rooms. Businesses can access offices tailored to their requirements, including secure private units within a shared infrastructure.
This allows companies to maintain privacy while benefiting from flexible arrangements and opportunities to network with other businesses in the same building.
For companies entering a new market or expanding their operations, the model also reduces the need to set up and manage every aspect of an office independently.
Enterprise 2.0: Beyond the desk
Khedia believes the next phase of office development will focus more closely on employees' everyday needs.
This could include access to healthcare, childcare, food and other facilities within or near office buildings. Such amenities can make workplaces more convenient while helping businesses attract and retain talent.
For Khedia, Enterprise 2.0 is about moving beyond conventional office layouts to create workplaces that support employees throughout the working day.
As companies reconsider their real estate needs, flexibility, collaboration, and employee experience are becoming important factors in deciding what an office should offer.

articles.title: Irlanda multó a Tinder con 11 millones de euros por entregar copias incompletas de los datos de sus usuarios
articles.text:
La Comisión de Protección de Datos de Irlanda multó con 11 millones de euros a la empresa que opera Tinder en Europa, porque la herramienta “Descargar mis datos” de la aplicación entregaba a los usuarios una copia incompleta de su información personal. El organismo anunció la decisión el 13 de noviembre de 2026.
El regulador también emitió una amonestación y ordenó a la empresa, MTCH Technology Services, adaptar el tratamiento de los datos a las normas europeas en un plazo de tres meses. Según el comunicado, algunas categorías de información se omitieron sin avisar al usuario y otras se entregaron solo en forma de resumen.
La herramienta se presentaba como una vía para obtener una copia de los datos de Tinder. Graham Doyle, comisionado adjunto del organismo, señaló que “decenas de miles de usuarios” la utilizaron durante el período que analizó la investigación.
Doyle sostuvo que este tipo de herramientas automáticas pueden ser “una vía útil y eficiente” para que las personas ejerzan sus derechos. A la vez, precisó que no tienen que ofrecer una copia completa, pero sí ser justas y transparentes sobre el alcance de lo que entregan.
La decisión la firmaron los comisionados Des Hogan, Dale Sunderland y Niamh Sweeney. El organismo agradeció en su comunicado la cooperación de otras autoridades europeas de protección de datos que participaron en el caso.
Una investigación abierta hace casi seis años
La Comisión inició el caso por iniciativa propia en enero de 2020, y no a partir de la denuncia de un usuario. Actuó como autoridad principal en Europa para la empresa, según el comunicado. La agencia Reuters describió a MTCH como la unidad irlandesa de Match Group, el grupo estadounidense dueño de Tinder.
La decisión se apoya en el artículo 15, apartado 3, del reglamento europeo de protección de datos. Esa norma obliga a quien guarda información personal a entregar una copia a la persona que la pide. El organismo no cuestionó que exista una herramienta automática para hacerlo, sino que prometiera más de lo que entregaba.
Match Group respondió que apelará. “Tinder colaboró con la Comisión durante toda la investigación y respaldamos las protecciones de privacidad que hemos construido para nuestros usuarios”, dijo un portavoz de la empresa.
Lo que el regulador no precisó
El comunicado no indica qué categorías de datos faltaban en las copias, ni qué período abarcó el análisis, ni si la información omitida estaba disponible por otra vía. Tampoco detalla el formato en que la herramienta entregaba los archivos.
PPC Land, un medio especializado en publicidad digital, señaló que el criterio alcanza a cualquier empresa que atienda pedidos de datos mediante una descarga automática en lugar de una respuesta manual. Esa lectura es del medio y no del regulador, que limitó su decisión a Tinder.
La Comisión declaró que publicará la decisión completa “en su momento”, sin fijar fecha. Hasta entonces, el plazo de tres meses para corregir la herramienta corre mientras Match Group prepara su apelación.
Qué derechos tienen los usuarios cuando piden sus datos a una plataforma
El derecho de acceso permite pedir a una compañía confirmación sobre el tratamiento de datos, una copia de la información y detalles sobre sus fines, destinatarios y categorías. La primera copia debe entregarse sin costo. La normativa europea exige una respuesta sin demoras indebidas y, en principio, dentro de un mes desde la solicitud presentada.
Si una empresa rechaza la petición, debe explicar los motivos e informar la posibilidad de presentar una reclamación ante la autoridad de protección de datos y de acudir a la Justicia. El Reglamento General de Protección de Datos admite ampliar la respuesta hasta dos meses adicionales cuando la complejidad o cantidad de solicitudes lo justifique.

articles.title: De 'GTA V' a 'GTA VI': 13 años, 4.700 empleados y una industria que sigue apartándose del camino de Rockstar
articles.text:
'Grand Theft Auto VI' sale este 19 de noviembre, 13 añazos después de que 'GTA V' llegara a las tiendas. En ese tiempo, Rockstar ha casi duplicado su plantilla, ha dejado de publicar juegos con la frecuencia de antaño y ha construido lo que probablemente será el videojuego más caro de la historia y algo, posiblemente, irrepetible durante mucho tiempo.
Han cambiado muchas cosas en esos 13 años, pero lo que no ha cambiado es que el lanzamiento de un GTA es un agujero negro para el calendario.
Por las nubes. Antes de iniciar el recorrido, vamos con lo que se espera. Take- Two, la empresa a la que pertenece Rockstar, presentó resultados el 9 de noviembre y el CEO, Strauss Zelnick, comentó que las reservas van "muy por encima de lo esperado". No dan cifras, pero tampoco parece que se necesit3en para anticipar que 'GTA VI' va a ser un juego que rompa récords.
La matriz prevé unas reservas netas de entre 8.000 y 8.200 millones de dólares en su ejercicio hasta marzo de 2027. Este dato es importante porque, en el ejercicio anterior, la cifra fue de 6.720 millones de dólares. Es decir, esperan un 20% más gracias al impulso del juego de Rockstar que llegará, recordemos, sin la gran mina que es el modo online.
Es, en definitiva, un lanzamiento enorme para la compañía y para la industria, pero esto no ha venido de la nada.
GTA V y el cambio de chip. Para medir el cambio de Rockstar que comentaba hace unos párrafos, toca mirar atrás. Entre octubre de 2003 y octubre de 2005, Rockstar publicó ocho juegos, entre los que se encontraba el mítico 'GTA San Andreas'. Luego vino 'GTA IV' en 2008, sus expansiones y, entre 2010 y 2013, aunque se calmaron un poco, siguieron a gran juego por año.
'Red Dead Redemption' en 2010, 'L.A. Noire' en 2011 y 'Max Payne 3' en 2012. Pero luego llegó 'GTA V', y con este cambió absolutamente todo. Take-Two anunció que facturó 800 millones de dólares en su primer día y más de 1.000 millones en los tres primeros. Marcó un récord para cualquier producto de entretenimiento hasta entonces y también fue una de las producciones más caras: 265 millones de dólares según las estimaciones de la época.
Sólo Rockstar puede afrontarlo. Luego vino el Online y, después, a vivir de las rentas. Entre 2013 y 2026, Rockstar sólo ha lanzado un juego original: 'Red Dead Redemption 2' en 2018. Fue otro éxito en ventas, pero mucho más modesto que el titán de 'GTA V' que la compañía lanzó en numerosas plataformas a lo largo de los años:
- PS4 y Xbox One en 2014.
- PC en 2015.
- PS5 y Xbox Series en 2022.
Cada plataforma extra significaba mayor base instalada, mayores ganancias por ventas directas y mayores tajadas por las microtransacciones del 'GTA Online'. En una filtración reciente se pudo ver que, 'GTA Online' en PC tendría 894.621 jugadores semanales que aportan 264.273 dólares a Rockstar, Xbox One tendría 1.129.023 jugadores gastando 1.867.947 dólares y PS5 contaría con 3.474.021 aportando 4.486.346 dólares a las arcas cada semana. Un millón al día, básicamente. Esto varía, claro, pero no deja de ser un dineral semanal durante años y años.
'Project Americas'. Las más de 220 millones de copias, unido a las ganancias del online, han permitido que Rockstar se tome con muchísima calma el desarrollo de este 'GTA VI' ambientado en Miami, aunque en un principio iba a ser aún más ambicioso. Hay pocos detalles sobre cómo se ha desarrollado el juego y, realmente, los más extensos vienen del reciente reportaje en Bloomberg en el que, tras pasar un día en Rockstar North, el periodista Jason Schreier dio algunas pinceladas de cómo iba a ser el juego en un principio.
Durante los primeros compases del desarrollo, se llamaba 'Project Americas' y pretendía abarcar buena parte de Norteamérica y Sudamérica. Esa ambición se fue reduciendo poco a poco tras viajes de investigación a Miami y debido a que el proceso de cerrar 'Red Dead Redemtpion 2' absorbió a casi toda la compañía. Fue cuando saltaron los escándalos de la cultura de crunch en el estudio y cuando se vio que, quizá, ni Rockstar ni ninguna compañía podía llevar dos juegos de esa escala en paralelo.
Cuando lanzaron el western, el desarrollo se aceleró. A finales de 2019 se fijó la historia de los dos protagonistas, pero seguía habiendo puntos clave que no se habían definido y luego llegó la pandemia, las contrataciones salvajes y una toma de decisión que se complicó debido a una dirección dividida entre tres personas y a la salida del estudio de Dan Houser (uno de los fundadores) y otros pesos pesados.
Ambición que tiene un precio. Para lograr lo que querían, Rockstar se puso a contratar. De los 2.441 empleados que lanzaron 'Red Dead Redemption 2', el estudio pasó a 4.711 empleados distribuidos en una docena de oficina. Esta cifra incluye toda la compañía, claro, pero es interesante comprobar cómo son prácticamente el doble de un juego a otro. Tienen un estudio para animación, otro dedicado a zonas concretas como Rockstar India y otro dedicado únicamente a los personajes no controlables.
Es una barbaridad e incluso hay fuentes que recogen cifras aún más abultadas, de picos de 5.900 empleados en algunos momentos. Esto, claro, no es oficial, al igual que ocurre con el presupuesto. Los juegos se han vuelto algo carísimo de hacer porque necesitan muchísimas personas y tiempo, y eso hay que pagarlo. Los 300 millones ya son habituales en grandes lanzamientos estadounidenses, pero durante un tiempo estuvo el rumor de que 'GTA VI' había costado (entre desarrollo y marketing) unos 2.000 millones.
Rockstar lo ha desmentido y las últimas estimaciones están entre los 1.000 y 1.500 millones en total. Sea la cifra que sea, lo que es evidente es que es el videojuego más caro hasta la fecha, y posiblemente el más caro en algo que nada tiene que ver con el dinero: el coste laboral.
Crunch y sindicato. Tras 'Red Dead Redemption 2', Rockstar empezó a aplicar políticas para reducir el crunch. Esto se refiere a las horas extra que se hacen en el desarrollo de videojuegos y que no es algo como "pues cada día, un par de horas más", no: hablamos de semanas de seis o incluso siete días, de jornadas dobles como si se trabajara en un hospital y de personas que tienen hijos durante el desarrollo y a los que prácticamente no ven durante meses.
Es, lamentablemente, algo muy habitual en la industria (el director de 'God of War' de 2018 lo expuso a la perfección en un documental) y es algo por lo que estudios como la desaparecida BioWare, Naughty Dog o la propia Rockstar se enorgullecen. O enorgullecían cuando no era un tema tan polémico y sensible, claro. Como digo, tras 'RDR 2', el estudio afirmó que había revisado sus políticas para evitar esa situación, pero los empleados han cuestionado la eficacia de esto.
Además del crunch, en octubre de 2025 se destapó otra polémica que aún colea: Rockstar despidió a una treintena de trabajadores en Reino Unido y Canadá por, según ellos, compartir información confidencial. Sin embargo, el sindicato IWGB sostiene que fue por actividad sindical, algo que ha llevado a la empresa a los tribunales de lo que aún no tenemos sentencia.
Filtraciones, en plural. Rockstar está obsesionada con la confidencialidad, pero no ha podido evitar ser víctima de dos de las filtraciones más brutales que ha experimentado la industria. La primera fue en septiembre de 2022, meses antes de la publicación del primer tráiler del juego, cuando una persona publicó 90 clips del desarrollo del juego. Se hizo con ellos gracias a un Fire TV Stick conectado a la tele de la habitación de un hotel y, según Rockstar, el ataque le costó cinco millones de dólares y miles de horas de trabajo a sus empleados.
En febrero de 2024, y con las filtraciones como argumento, la empresa canceló el teletrabajo, por lo que las condiciones de los empleados se deterioraron un poco más. Para colmo, a mediados de agosto de este año y a poco más de una semana de ver el primer gameplay del juego, alguien llamado 'Cyberleek' publicó vídeos e imágenes de 'GTA VI'. También tenía una build del título y poco a poco fue publicando más material. De esto no nos hicimos eco en Xataka porque, realmente, es algo que daña a los trabajadores del estudio y juega en contra de los mismos.
El hacker afirmó tener una misión, la de luchar por el formato físico (recordemos que 'GTA VI' no tiene formato físico y que justo este verano Sony anunció que se bajará del carro a partir de enero de 2028), pero fue sospechoso porque había una cripto ligada a toda la filtración y olía bastante a estafa. Al margen de esto, era evidente que la lucha contra las filtraciones no sirvió de mucho.
Nadie quiere coincidir. Pero bueno, visto todo esto, aquí estamos, a pocos días de poder poner nuestras manos sobre el juego más esperado. Y tenemos un calendario bastante limpio porque nadie quiere coincidir con un 'GTA'. Cuando salió 'GTA V', casi el 90% de las ventas de juego en Reino Unido durante la primera semana fueron para Rockstar. Ese reflejo, trece años después, se mantiene.
En 2025, cuando se esperaba el juego, Bloomberg ya contó que muchas editoras estaban esperando lo máximo posible para anunciar la fecha de sus lanzamientos. Nadie quería salir cerca de 'GTA VI' porque sabían que no se iba a hablar de otra cosa. Y, de hecho, hay ejemplos concretos como 'Fable', una de las grandes producciones de Microsoft que se movió a febrero del año que viene para no coincidir.
A Nintendo y Barbie les da igual. De hecho sólo hay que ver el calendario de lanzamientos para comprobar cómo prácticamente cada semana de este año se ha lanzado algo importante... excepto esta que acabamos de cerrar, la que viene y lo que queda de diciembre. Pero claro, siempre hay una nota discordante y, en este caso, tenemos dos.
Por un lado, el 'Barbie Rewind', al que le da exactamente igual el lanzamiento de 'GTA VI' y que ha protagonizado su propio momento 'Barbenheimer', subiéndose al meme de que todos temen el lanzamiento de 'GTA'... excepto Barbie. Por otro, Nintendo. 'GTA VI' no sale en Nintendo Switch 2 y, para la compañía japonesa, si algo no sale en su plataforma es, básicamente, como si no existiera.
Es una exageración, claro, pero van a su ritmo y, además, han lanzado el remake de 'The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time' que no sólo se ha convertido en uno de los juegos mejor valorados de la historia, sino uno que, en cinco días, ha vendido más de 5,2 millones de unidades.
Y después... qué. Va a ser curioso ver el recuento de las ventas iniciales de este 'GTA VI' y también las notas. Todos los anteriores están muy arriba en el recuento de notas y hay que esperar a ver en qué numerito en Metacritic se queda este juego que entrará por los pelos en los candidatos a llevarse el GOTY. Y si bien aún no hemos tenido 'GTA VI', ya hay quien se pregunta, visto lo visto, cuánto tendremos que esperar para un 'GTA VII'.
Paso a paso, ya que primero vendrá la versión de PC y lo que quieran hacer con el nuevo 'GTA Online', pero según Bloomberg, 'GTA VI' no sólo es un juego mastodóntico, sino la base de las herramientas y tecnología para los juegos futuros de Rockstar. Esto aceleraría la llegada de un nuevo juego de la compañía o de un nuevo 'GTA', pero es algo que sólo el tiempo dirá.

Black Friday 2026 – La tondeuse à gazon Dreame A1 Pro à 599,00 € (-19%)
La tondeuse à gazon Dreame A1 Pro passe sous les 600 € chez Amazon soit une baisse d'environ 19% sur le prix habituellement constaté. C'est actuellement l'un des meilleurs produit de notre comparatif.
Version améliorée du Dreame A1, le robot-tondeuse A1 Pro reprend en y ajoutant quelques raffinements les atouts du modèle original : tonte sans fil périphérique, cartographie 3D et app intuitive. Au programme, un revêtement plus résistant, des roues crantées pour une meilleure motricité et la gestion de deux zones de coupe.

Points forts
- Fonctionnement entièrement sans fil.

- Installation et configuration faciles.
Points faibles
- Détection d'obstacles parfois imprécise
- Tonte des bordures.

Le robot-tondeuse Dreame A1 Pro reprend les bases solides de l'A1 tout en corrigeant quelques points stratégiques. Ses roues crantées offrent une meilleure motricité, la gestion multicarte élargit les usages pour les jardins non contigus, tandis que la finition mate semble mieux pensée pour durer. On conserve une app complète, une navigation fiable sans fil périphérique et une tonte globalement homogène, malgré une gestion des angles et des bordures perfectible. En face de modèles plus chers ou plus complexes à installer, l'A1 Pro reste un choix pertinent pour ceux qui cherchent simplicité, efficacité et personnalisation, sans sacrifier à l’esthétique ou l’expérience utilisateur. À moins d’avoir un terrain très fragmenté ou des attentes poussées sur les finitions, c’est l’un des meilleurs rapports qualité/prix dans cette gamme.

articles.title: Thermal Grizzly Details WireView Pro II Extended GPU Warranty Conditions
articles.text:
Sunday, November 15th 2026
Thermal Grizzly Details WireView Pro II Extended GPU Warranty Conditions
Thermal Grizzly has published an FAQ clarifying the conditions of its WireView Pro II extended GPU warranty, covering cables, settings, adapters, and claims. Neither the USB cable nor the motherboard Y-splitter has to be connected for coverage. The Y-splitter lets the WireView shut the PC down through the power-button header, but Thermal Grizzly only recommends it. Monitoring has to stay enabled, though. Lowering the current, temperature, or power thresholds is fine, but raising them above the defaults or switching monitoring off is not.
Third-party extensions between the WireView and the GPU are allowed as long as each 12 V line stays separate. Adapters that bridge those lines internally stop the WireView from reading the current on each GPU power contact, so those builds aren't covered. A 90-degree connector isn't a problem by itself, since it comes down to the internal wiring. On the PSU side, cables approved for that exact PSU model are fine. Coverage runs for 24 months from the WireView purchase, even after the GPU's own warranty ends, but only for the original buyer with proof of purchase.The warranty covers damage to the 12VHPWR or 12V-2x6 connector and resulting GPU damage, not unrelated faults, PSUs, or other parts. Shunt mods, XOC BIOS with a raised power target, and commercial mining are excluded. Accepted claims start with a repair, and if that doesn't work, Thermal Grizzly sends a card with comparable performance, though not necessarily the same brand or edition. Owners who spot melting are advised to power down, unplug the PSU, leave the connector attached, take photos, and contact support before shipping anything.

articles.title: TechCrunch Mobility: The Nvidia backup plan for China's self-driving industry | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Welcome back to TechCrunch Mobility, your hub for the future of transportation and now, more than ever, the role AI is playing in it. To get this in your inbox, sign up here for free — just click TechCrunch Mobility!
I am traveling through Portugal now that Web Summit has wrapped up, so please enjoy this shortened edition.
Web Summit leaned heavily into Chinese founders and companies this year. The opening remarks from Web Summit co-founder Paddy Cosgrave drove the point home when he said the superstars of the future are coming from China, not California. He also gave a strong endorsement of China and open source technology when he noted that Chinese companies are building more of our shared future than anyone else.
These remarks carried a different kind of weight just a few days later as the news spread throughout the conference that Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang had resigned from his leadership post after admitting to an affair with an alleged spy.
The former CEO, after all, has been one of the strongest proponents for open source in the United States. And anyone who has followed the emergence of autonomous vehicle tech knows how central Nvidia is to that ecosystem.
Nvidia is a major supplier of AI computing technology to the industry — although the degree of reliance varies. Some companies are using Nvidia’s automotive processors to run automated driving software, while others are using Nvidia GPUs to train autonomous driving models. And then there are the full-stack partnerships, which includes Mercedes-Benz, Zoox, and Wayve.
I spoke to Leo Wang, the CFO of Chinese autonomous vehicle company Pony.ai, this week. I asked him about the challenges China’s self-driving industry faces and what he thinks will happen if the fallout from Huang’s resignation results in even stricter export controls on Nvidia chips shipped to China.
Demand is already far greater than supply, Wang said, noting that it’s one of the pain points Pony.ai struggles with. The company’s strategy is twofold. Engineers are directed to be as efficient as possible when deploying its training models. That might mean using midtier compute resources instead of high-end ones, he said.
Pony.ai is also turning more to domestically produced chips to help close the gap.
“If you look at the whole ecosystem, especially in recent years, definitely domestic chips in China also get lots of attention and development,” he said, noting that these chips provide another option for AI training. “I think that gives us some flexibility.”
When asked what he thinks will happen if export restrictions on Nvidia chips tighten, Wang said Chinese companies have already been preparing.
“If you look at the whole situation, this has been developing for already a couple of years,” he said. “Everyone, I would say, is also practicing kind of like a Plan B for a few years, so at least if you think about that, I would say there are alternatives. Although cost-effectiveness-wise, probably it’s not the best choice yet. But still, it’s an alternative way that already exists and which is more mature than a few years ago.”
Deals!
May Mobility plans to use the Volkswagen all-electric ID. Buzz for its global ride-hailing platform. The company said it is targeting the deployment of more than 10,000 autonomous vehicles through 2031. This does not mean that VW’s MOIA group is ditching Mobileye, I have been told. Instead, VW told me, the company is offering an automated driving-ready base vehicle to other companies that develop their own self-driving systems. (This was just presented last month during Nvidia GTC in Berlin.)
Newmo, a Japanese robotaxi startup, raised a ¥20.8 billion (roughly $135 million) round led by KDDI.
ParkBee, a Dutch parking technology company, acquired Mobian’s city and parking operations.
Port, an urban logistics company, raised €14.5 million in a round led by the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) and Balnord.
Notable reads and other tidbits
Lucid reported Q3 revenue of $350 million, below Wall Street expectations, and it is still losing money. Although its Q3 net loss did narrow to $830.9 million. Notably, the EV maker increased its delayed draw term loan from its largest shareholder, Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, to $1.75 billion.
The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration is investigating a Waymo software recall from a year ago that was issued after numerous reports that its robotaxis were illegally passing school buses. The agency said that a majority of these reported incidents occurred after the company deployed a software update intended to fix the problem. Sources familiar with Waymo tell me that there have not been school bus-related incidents since March. I have not been able to independently verify that with the Austin Independent School District.
The Tesla Cybertruck will live on through next summer, but production will ultimately end, according to Elon Musk, who defended the polarizing steel-clad truck.
Tesla is expanding its robotaxi service to San Antonio, Texas, as it seeks to compete with Waymo and position itself as more than just an automaker.
Uber is launching a new service that lets customers reserve and pay for parking in major U.S. cities, about nine months after the ride-hailing company acquired parking app SpotHero. Meanwhile, the company is notifying thousands of drivers that their personal and driver’s license information was stolen during an October data breach at one of the company’s tech providers.
United Airlines will restrict access to AI agents seeking to book flights and manage reservations on their users’ behalf.

articles.title: Drying washing inside doesn’t have to mean wet windows and musty jumpers — these smart tips will get your clothes dry faster, without making your home damp
articles.text:
Drying laundry indoors this winter? Follow these expert tips to banish damp smells, condensation, and mould without sending your energy bills soaring
Sometimes, particularly during the cold months, drying laundry indoors is the practical choice. Some garments are too delicate for a tumble dryer; you may be trying to reduce your energy usage, or you may not have a dryer at all.
However, drying clothes inside also greatly increases the humidity in your home, leading to condensation and mould. You might find that your clothes dry too slowly as well, resulting in an unpleasant musty smell. This is even more likely in the winter, when you’re likely to keep windows closed and may limit your use of central heating to keep bills down.
Thankfully, there are ways to dry your clothes more quickly without spiking your energy bill. Chris Michael, co-founder of Meaco, has offered some tips to help this winter:
Start with an extra spin
Give laundry a second spin in the washing machine to extract more water before hanging it up. This leaves less moisture in the fabric to evaporate during drying.
Hang washing up promptly
Empty the machine as soon as the cycle finishes to help prevent damp smells developing in clothes and the drum.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Choose the right drying space
Use a warm, well-ventilated room. Keep the internal door closed to limit moisture spreading through the home, while providing a route for it to escape outside.
Leave space between garments
Use an airer rather than draping washing over radiators. Avoid overlapping clothes and use hangers for any items that will not fit comfortably on the rack. Gaps between garments allow air to circulate and help them dry more quickly.
Arrange the airer carefully
Position the rack away from walls to prevent moisture from becoming trapped. Place smaller items towards the bottom and larger garments at the top, maintaining space for airflow throughout the load.
Let moisture escape
When drying laundry without a dehumidifier, open a window where possible to let moisture escape, although some warmth will escape too.
Limit other sources of humidity
Keep lids on saucepans when cooking and use an extractor or open a window when bathing or showering. Open bedroom windows briefly in the morning to let out the moisture accumulated overnight from breathing. These everyday changes reduce the additional moisture entering the air while laundry dries.
Invest in a dehumidifier
A dehumidifier removes moisture from the clothes, so laundry can dry indoors without opening windows and losing heat, and without the running costs of a tumble dryer. There is an upfront cost, but a dehumidifier saves you money over time. For example, a Meaco Arete One 10L costs approx. 24p to dry a load of washing compared to £1.01 per load for a conventional tumble dryer. If used 270 times a year, that’s a saving of over £200.

articles.title: 3D printing dev’s free tool unlocks curved printing along all three axes — PancakeSlicer makes non-planar curved 3D printing accessible, potentially leading to rapid community development
articles.text:
3D printing dev’s free tool unlocks curved printing along all three axes — PancakeSlicer makes non-planar curved 3D printing accessible, potentially leading to rapid community development
Non-planar 3D printing has mostly been experimental, but PancakeSlicer could finally make more people interested in trying it out and find more ways to improve it and use it practically.
Alpaca Engineering posted a YouTube video yesterday showcasing his self-hostable non-planar slicer. He explains that most non-planar 3D printing — printing across all three axes, rather than in 2D horizontal layers — demonstrations are usually for research purposes, for demonstration and experimentation, with no easy way for most 3D printer owners to try out non-planar 3D printing. His project, named PancakeSlicer, aims to fix this by making his non-planar slicing algorithm as easy to implement as existing slicing workflows, even improving upon it with 3D printer management features.
Alpaca Engineering explains that every few months, a non-planar 3D printing demonstration goes viral, but is rarely adopted practically by most 3D printer owners. Most non-planar experiments are for research, with half-abandoned GitHub projects. He further explains that non-planar isn’t widely adopted not because there aren’t any general-purpose non-planar slicers, but because it’s not accessible and easily implemented in a familiar workflow, with 3D printer owners spoiled by modern workflows and not needing to manually run G-code directly from an SD card.
Commercially available 3D printers are also not optimized for non-planar 3D printing. The challenge with printing at various angles is the clearance angle needed to bring a print head up and down without crashing into its own print. The slicer uses 3D models of various print heads from different 3D printer models to know how to slice the object to avoid collisions, thus having limited support; but Alpaca Engineering has listed a large number of supported 3D printers from Bambu Lab, Prusa, Creality, Voron, and many others. The varying shapes of the print heads also mean different printers will have different capabilities, with some managing less angle and curvature than others.
Alpaca Engineering also has great animations and practical demonstrations of the different slicing algorithms in the slicer, including how the algorithm slices the object for non-planar printing. We highly suggest you watch the video if you’re interested, as his animations explain non-planar slicing intuitively.
One of the best features of this slicer is its self-hosting features. Users can host the slicer from a desktop, NAS, or a home server and access it with a web UI, allowing multiple users to send print jobs from any device. It also has 3D printer management features, applying different profiles to different printer brands, unifying the experience without hopping from one slicer to another to operate multiple 3D printers — this is even available to Bambu Lab users, replacing Bambu Studio and Bambu Connect in LAN-only mode. The slicer can also manage two slice jobs at the same time in case other users happen to be slicing at the same time.
While PancakeSlicer isn’t the first to implement self-hosted 3D printer management features, it certainly levels up his initial goal of making non-planar slicing as easy to access as most modern workflows. We hope to see how more people can experiment with non-planar 3D printing, contribute their findings, and rapidly improve upon it as a genuinely practical slicing method.

Jhet Borja is a serial hobbyist who was taking apart toys from childhood and sketching inventions. He now loves doing DIY projects ranging from designing custom 3D-printed parts, building PCs and keyboards, all the way to woodworking. If he's not getting his hands dirty, he's probably brainstorming his next project.
