articles.title: Listen to this: Armand Hammer’s Snakes & Ladders
articles.text:
I open with this caveat: I haven’t had a ton of time to digest the surprise Armand Hammer record that dropped this week. Billy Woods and Elucid rarely miss, though, and my initial reaction is that Snakes & Ladders ranks among their best. It doesn’t have the seamless throughline production-wise that their collabs with Alchemist (Haram and Mercy) do, but it’s still clearly the singular vision of the two men at its center.
Listen to this: Armand Hammer’s Snakes & Ladders
Armand Hammer’s latest album is among their best.
Listen to this: Armand Hammer’s Snakes & Ladders
Armand Hammer’s latest album is among their best.
Ominous noises dance in the background, blasts of noise add dashes of industrial rage, bass lines throb, and saxophone bleats call out to the sky. Woods and Elucid have always had excellent taste in production, but here they seem to have brought out the best in collaborators like clipping, Kenny Segal, and Child Actor. They’ve also successfully rallied them around a specific sound palette that keeps the record from actually sounding like it has beats from 11 different producers.
Of course, what makes Armand Hammer stand out from many of their contemporaries is their unique and verbose flows. Their lyrical mastery even makes guest rappers like $ilkmoney, who you can practically hear stalking around the mic as he seethes on “Risk,” up their game.
On songs like “Gravity,” Billy Woods navigates burgeoning romance with shocking directness, while also acknowledging obliquely how hard it can be to say what you mean.
Get it off your chest or put it to the side
As a preface, all due respect, I suggest
‘Cause it’s nothing more precious than time
On “Vespers,” he references Siouxsie and the Banshees and says “My nightcap three fingers of Fernet,” which is probably the first time I’ve ever heard Fernet Branca get a shoutout in a rap song.
“Graveside” is another highlight where it’s Elucid’s turn to get vulnerable:
I see you in the grave, I see you in the dirt
Shouts and hollers every which way, hurting
Darkness chase light
Steel shut close curtain
In some ways, this record feels like a culmination of what Billy Woods and Elucid have been working towards on their non-Alchemist-produced Armand Hammer records like We Buy Diabetic Test Strips, but also their recent solo records like Golliwog and Revelator.
Armand Hammer’s Snakes & Ladders is available on Bandcamp and most major streaming services, including Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube Music, Qobuz, and Deezer.

articles.title: 4 horas de sono estão boas pra você? Genética pode ajudar a explicar quem precisa de menos sono
articles.text:
Mutações genéticas raras podem explicar por que algumas pessoas funcionam bem dormindo apenas de quatro a seis horas e meia por noite, sem apresentar os prejuízos habituais da falta de sono.
Enquanto a Fundação Nacional do Sono dos Estados Unidos recomenda de sete a nove horas diárias para adultos de 26 a 64 anos, cientistas investigam como a genética influencia essas diferenças.
O que é o sono curto natural familiar
Um exemplo estudado pela ciência é a professora de imunologia Aimee Pugh Bernard, da Universidade do Colorado, nos Estados Unidos. Ela costuma dormir perto das 22h e acordar por volta das 4h30 com energia para passear com o cachorro, treinar por uma hora na academia e trabalhar por uma hora e meia antes das 8h. Seu pai e seu irmão apresentam uma rotina semelhante.
Em 2019, Bernard descobriu ser portadora de uma mutação associada ao sono curto natural familiar (FNSS, na sigla em inglês). A condição hereditária faz com que algumas pessoas durmam naturalmente entre quatro e seis horas e meia por noite. Para confirmar a suspeita, ela enviou uma amostra de sangue à equipe de pesquisadores da Universidade da Califórnia em São Francisco.
Segundo a bióloga molecular Ying-Hui Fu, principal pesquisadora da equipe, os motivos pelos quais os portadores do FNSS parecem funcionar bem dormindo pouco ainda são investigados. Experimentos liderados por ela em 2019 indicaram que camundongos com uma dessas variantes dormiam menos e apresentavam proteção contra déficits de memória. Em outro teste, animais portadores de determinadas variantes tiveram menor probabilidade de desenvolver uma forma de Alzheimer característica da espécie.
Um estudo internacional de 2014 com gêmeos fraternos também encontrou diferenças. O irmão portador da mutação dormia cerca de uma hora a menos, mas mantinha praticamente a mesma duração de sono profundo. Após 38 horas acordado, registrou aproximadamente 40% menos falhas de rendimento que o irmão.
Nem toda predisposição genética protege
Calcula-se que o tempo de sono seja hereditário em 30% a 65%. Uma análise ainda em fase de pré-publicação, liderada pela geneticista Isabelle Austin-Zimmerman, do King’s College de Londres, avaliou dados de quase 650 mil adultos e identificou cerca de 244 regiões do genoma associadas à duração do descanso. Isoladamente, cada variante comum está relacionada a uma diferença de aproximadamente um minuto. Seus efeitos combinados podem explicar variações de cerca de 20 minutos.
Essas alterações, porém, não representam necessariamente uma vantagem. Pesquisas identificaram diferentes associações entre predisposição genética a dormir pouco e condições de saúde:
- Insônia e outros problemas: variantes relacionadas à menor duração do sono foram associadas a maior risco de cansaço, TDAH, sintomas depressivos e diabetes tipo 2. Os resultados não comprovam relação de causa e efeito.
- Psicose pós-parto: um estudo com 343 mulheres com transtorno bipolar que haviam dado à luz encontrou metade do risco da condição entre aquelas com maior predisposição genética a precisar de pouco sono. A pesquisa foi liderada pela ginecologista e obstetra Chiara Petrosellini, do University College de Londres.
- Deterioração cognitiva: em um experimento com adultos saudáveis, limitar o tempo na cama a quatro ou seis horas por duas semanas provocou queda progressiva no rendimento dos participantes, embora eles relatassem apenas leve sonolência.
O último resultado ajuda a explicar por que a percepção individual nem sempre revela os efeitos da privação de sono. “Sua capacidade se deteriora cada vez mais, mas, ao mesmo tempo, você tem cada vez menos consciência dessa deterioração”, explica Hans van Dongen, pesquisador do Centro de Pesquisa do Sono e Rendimento da Universidade Estadual de Washington.
Potencial para futuros medicamentos
Compreender como essas variações genéticas funcionam poderá ajudar a indústria farmacêutica a desenvolver tratamentos para transtornos do sono ou produtos que permitam aos militares passar o dia com menos horas de descanso.
Fu ressalta, porém, que é necessário identificar os mecanismos envolvidos antes de avançar nessa direção. Sem esse conhecimento, existe o risco de provocar consequências indesejadas a longo prazo. “Você não irá querer dormir menos e, depois de cinco, 10 ou 20 anos, acabar desenvolvendo Alzheimer, Parkinson ou câncer”, afirma.
Para Bernard, descobrir a origem genética de sua característica trouxe alívio. Antes, ela se perguntava se tinha dificuldade para relaxar ou se tentava assumir tarefas demais. Agora, a professora entende melhor seu padrão de sono: “Sei que, geneticamente, é assim que sou. E simplesmente precisarei aceitar isso”.
Valdir Antonelli é jornalista com especialização em marketing digital e consumo.

articles.title: Today I learned why wind farms paint one turbine blade black
articles.text:
Today I learned why wind farms paint one turbine blade black
And why newer offshore farms are now trying red
You'd think that painting a single turbine blade black is a pretty inexpensive fix for accidental bird deaths. It sounds almost too good to be true, which perhaps it is.
At the Smøla wind farm in Norway, every wind turbine had one of its blade painted black for an extended science experiment back in August 2013. Over the next three years, the number of bird carcasses found fell by 70%.
However, similar experiments in the Netherlands did not yield positive results, because apparently this fix depends heavily on the local bird species and population size.
Too many dead birds
There are a total of 68 turbines at the Smøla wind power plant, an archipelago off the coast of Central Norway. Researchers from the Norwegian Institute for Nature Research compared four regular turbines with four neighboring ones that had one blade painted black for this experiment.
They regularly counted the number of bird carcasses within 100 meters of the wind farm. This continued over a period of more than ten years, combining 7.5 years of baseline data from before painting any turbine blades to 3.5 years of data from after. In 2020, they published their findings in a paper called Ecology and Evolution.
Turns out that this small change in visual cues reduced the number of bird deaths by over 70%, proving especially effective on the somewhat rare white-tailed sea eagle population of the region. While the researchers noted that this anecdotal data may not hold up to different bird populations, this was still independent real-world confirmation of a separate laboratory experiment that found similar results in 2003.
How a black blade is supposed to help
What difference does one black blade make? According to researchers, it has to do with how birds process visual cues.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Animation designers call it motion smearing, where images that move too fast for the human eye to follow are inferred in the brain as one continuous motion. When turbine blades are in motion, birds find it difficult to notice the threat because the unicolor rotating blades look like one giant circle.
When you paint one of these blades black, it breaks up the pattern so the moving blades are more easily distinguishable to the eye. But as Audubon reported, these are preliminary findings that won't translate to all bird species equally — especially ones that don't have the visual acuity to notice the difference. There's also a significant amount of effort involved, since painting turbines in operation requires both lifts and specialist crews who can navigate the height.
When the trick stops working
Most of the land experiments so far have stuck with black, but at sea, a new trial is experimenting with a different color.
Dutch consortium Ecowende is fitting seven Vestas V236-15.0 MW turbines with one red 115.5-meter blade each. Red was chosen after weighing options against criteria such as durability and heat management, apart from the obvious benefit of being more easily discernible from a distance.
That said, seabirds may generally need less help than expected. A Vattenfall and Spoor study at its Aberdeen offshore wind farm tracked 2,007 flight paths over 19 months. It found no confirmed collisions, with birds typically keeping 100 to 200 meters away.

These days, most of his work revolves around B2B software, such as AI website builders, VoIP platforms, and CRMs, among other things. articles.title: Vulcan rocket fails, destroying 40 Amazon Leo satellites
articles.text:
United Launch Alliance (ULA) suffered what is reportedly its first mission failure in its 20-year history, failing to deliver 40 Amazon Leo satellites to orbit. Leo is Amazon’s competitor to SpaceX’s Starlink, but it has struggled to get off the ground so far, putting only a small portion of the necessary satellites to challenge Starlink into orbit. Today’s launch was supposed to be the first of 38 flights Amazon purchased from ULA.
Vulcan rocket fails, destroying 40 Amazon Leo satellites
ULA said an ‘anomaly’ led to its Vulcan vehicle failing to deliver its payload to orbit.
In a statement posted on X, ULA said, “Based on data received by our Launch Director, we confirm that the Vulcan vehicle launched from Space Launch Complex 41 suffered an anomaly 10 minutes into the flight and failed to deliver the Amazon mission to orbit.”
The company said it was currently unclear what caused the failure, but pledged transparency as it continues its investigation. Amazon projected confidence in its launch partner despite the failure, posting on X that, “ There is risk with any launch, and that’s especially true for inaugural missions like LV-01. ULA has been a trusted partner for Amazon, and we believe they’ll learn from this mission and deliver on their long-term plans for Vulcan.”

articles.title: Wettlauf zum Mond: Warum China ganz anders plant als die USA
articles.text:
Während die Nasa schon Astronauten ins All schickt: Warum China bei seinen Mond-Tests vorerst auf Menschen verzichtet
Fast 60 Jahre nach der ersten Mondlandung eines Menschen ist ein neuer Wettlauf der Nationen entbrannt, an dem sich auch China beteiligt. Anstatt bemannte Probeflüge durchzuführen, will Raumfahrtbehörde CNSA allerdings zunächst auf unbemannte Vehikel setzen. Laut dem unabhängigen X-Account CNSpaceflight, der regelmäßig Updates aus der chinesischen Raumfahrt postet, soll die erste von vier geplanten Missionen im Jahr 2027 stattfinden. Die erste bemannte Landung sei demnach noch vor 2030 geplant. Damit hält die chinesische Raumfahrtbehörde den Druck auf die USA aufrecht. Die Nasa will im Rahmen des Artemis-Programms voraussichtlich 2028 erstmals wieder Astronaut:innen auf den Mond bringen. Das Vorhaben wurde aber bereits mehrere Male verschoben.
Roboterbasierte Testflüge zum Mond
Laut CNSpaceflight soll das unbemannte Raumschiff „Mengzhou” zunächst für Tests in die niedrige Erdumlaufbahn starten. Die moderne Besatzungskapsel, die übersetzt „Traumschiff“ heißt, könnte künftig auch chinesische Astronaut:innen befördern. Die zweite Mission ist für 2028 geplant und soll eine noch leistungsstärkere Rakete nutzen. Auch dieser Flug bleibt unbemannt und markiert das Debüt der Rakete „Long March-10“, die die Landefähre „Lanyue“ in die Mondumlaufbahn bringen soll. Die dritte Mission soll 2029 stattfinden und zielt ebenfalls auf eine unbemannte Mondlandung ab. Sie umfasst zwei Starts von „Long March-10“ – jeweils einen mit „Mengzhou” und „Lanyue”.
Ziel der roboterbasierten Testflüge sei es, die eigentliche Mission vorzubereiten. Laut CNSpaceflight sollen letztlich drei Astronaut:innen an Bord einer „Mengzhou“-Kapsel starten. Zwei von ihnen sollen in „Lanyue“ umsteigen, auf dem Mond landen und dort drei Tage verbringen. Der Zeitplan dürfte nicht zufällig gewählt sein, denn das Jahr 2029 fällt mit dem 80. Jahrestag der aktuellen Regierung zusammen. Gleichzeitig bietet die Formulierung „vor 2030“ genug Flexibilität für den Fall, dass etwas nicht nach Plan verläuft.
Wie die Robotikindustrie profitiert
Die Strategie der chinesischen Raumfahrtbehörde CNSA unterscheidet sich deutlich von der der Nasa, die auf bemannte Testflüge setzt. Im April schickte Artemis II vier Astronaut:innen um den Mond. Nächstes Jahr wird die vierköpfige Besatzung von Artemis III etwa zwei Wochen in der Erdumlaufbahn verbringen und das Andocken an zwei kommerzielle Landefähren üben. Trotz dieses Unterschieds setzen auch die USA auf Robotik, wie unter anderem Mashable berichtet.
China erklärt, dass die unbemannten Missionen die erste bemannte Landung sicherer machen würden. Der Fokus auf Robotik soll aber auch den technologischen Führungsanspruch des Landes sichtbar machen. Denn der Wettbewerb mit den USA betrifft nicht nur die Mondlandung – sondern auch den Bau moderner Robotersysteme. Chinas Mondprogramm stärkt die heimische Industrie, da es ihr Großaufträge verschafft und zugleich als Testumgebung dient, um Systeme für Bergbau oder Logistik unter extremen Bedingungen zu erproben.
Chinesische Robotikindustrie schwächelt
Das Land gilt derzeit als Vorreiter – trotzdem bleibt der wirtschaftliche Erfolg bei vielen chinesischen Robotikunternehmen bisher aus. Besonders bei der humanoiden Robotik hat China deshalb zuletzt auf die Bremse getreten. Wie The Verge im Dezember 2025 berichtete, warnte ein Sprecher der Nationalen Entwicklungs- und Reformkommission vor einer „Robotik-Blase“. Das könnte auch die Investitionen beeinflusst haben: Laut Bloomberg sanken diese im September 2026 um mehr als 40 Prozent.

articles.title: 5 posibles escenarios que podría enfrentar el 'Universo DC' en adelante (y cinco riesgos que corre)
articles.text:
DC se encuentra otra vez en medio de la incertidumbre. Luego de la salida de James Gunn y Peter Safran, el universo cinematográfico de la editorial pasa por momentos complicados. Mucho más parece otra vez enfrentar el terreno resbaladizo y riesgoso de un reboot. Pero además, se trata quizás de una coyuntura que demuestra que Skydance (antigua Warner) comienza a plantear un camino. El de construir una franquicia al estilo del Universo Cinematográfico de Marvel.
Hacerlo, además, tomando el ejemplo de la saga de poner en el centro de sus proyectos a los personajes más importantes de su mitología. Para eso, Skydance contrató a Jeremy Latcham, veterano de Marvel y productor de varios de sus éxitos tempranos como Iron Man (2008). Pero en realidad, lo que parece una decisión empresarial, tiene un claro enfoque creativo. Por lo que buena parte del trabajo de James Gunn quedará descartado o será sensiblemente modificado.
Para explorar en el tema, te dejamos los cinco escenarios que podría transitar el Universo de DC. Todo, bajo la nueva dirección de un hombre que, además, ya admitió tener valores conservadores. También te incluimos los cinco riesgos más críticos que amenazan la estabilidad de la franquicia. Una exploración acerca de lo que la saga puede esperar de ahora en más, luego de este nuevo golpe de timón que reformula de nuevo a DC.
Cinco escenarios futuros para DC
El retorno al modelo de franquicias tradicionales e independientes
Con la llegada de Jeremy Latcham, un veterano formado en la estructura clásica de Hollywood, DC Studios podría hacer específicos cambios. El más notorio, abandonar la obsesión por un universo masivo y rígidamente interconectado. En su lugar, el estudio optaría por un modelo centrado en franquicias individuales de alta calidad que funcionen por mérito propio.
Bajo este enfoque, sagas como el Batman de Matt Reeves o el Superman de James Gunn tendrían sus propias subfranquicias. Eso, sin la presión de cruzarse constantemente en eventos masivos. Esto daría a los directores mayor libertad creativa y reduciría la fatiga del espectador. Por lo que ya no se vería obligado a consumir múltiples series de televisión y películas derivadas para comprender una trama principal.
El reciclaje estructural del plan original de James Gunn
Aunque James Gunn y Peter Safran dejaron el control ejecutivo, su aporte podría no desaparecer del todo. Eso, debido a la enorme cantidad de material ya escrito, filmado o planificado. Una inversión que Skydance no puede descartar por completo.
En este escenario, el estudio mantendría el esqueleto narrativo diseñado por Gunn, pero con una ejecución mucho más conservadora y supervisada. Latcham asumiría el rol de editor corporativo, filtrando los elementos más extravagantes, excéntricos o experimentales. Todo, para adaptarlos a un tono más accesible y comercial.
Un reinicio suave centrado exclusivamente en la Trinidad de DC
En el peor de los casos, la nueva administración podría ejecutar un control de daños drástico. Esto implicaría cancelar discretamente las producciones menos avanzadas y concentrar todos los recursos económicos y creativos. Eso, para reiniciar de manera segura a los tres pilares de la editorial: Superman, Batman y Wonder Woman.
Este escenario priorizaría historias de escala clásica y blockbusters tradicionales dirigidos a audiencias masivas y familiares. Se dejaría atrás el tono experimental y la interconexión con producciones animadas o televisivas para enfocarse puramente en la gran pantalla. La Trinidad funcionaría como el motor comercial único de la marca, construyendo una mitología directa y sin ramificaciones confusas.
La canibalización o absorción por parte del ‘Elseworlds’ exitoso
Actualmente, los proyectos cinematográficos más estables y aclamados por la crítica de DC pertenecen al sello de historias independientes. Este conocido como Elseworlds, destacando el universo criminal de The Batman capitaneado por Matt Reeves.
Por lo que un escenario muy viable es que Skydance decida convertir la franquicia de Reeves en el verdadero eje central de su universo cinematográfico. Esto requeriría expandir ese universo realista e introducir versiones de Superman u otros metahumanos que encajen en dicho tono. De este modo, la marca dejaría de intentar construir un universo desde una base de fantasía colorida y cósmica. Todo para edificarlo sobre los cimientos de una saga cinematográfica que ya cuenta con el respeto de la crítica y el público.
La venta de licencias y diversificación de distribución a terceros
Ante los altos costos que implica mantener un estudio cinematográfico dedicado exclusivamente a superhéroes, Skydance podría tomar una decisión drástica. En lugar de financiar y producir internamente cada largometraje, DC Studios adoptaría un enfoque similar al de Sony con Spider-Man.
O la propia Marvel en los años noventa: licenciar personajes específicos a otros grandes estudios o plataformas de streaming. DC retendría los derechos principales y recibiría regalías masivas junto con derechos de distribución, pero descentralizaría la producción de contenido. Una solución interesante, aunque la menos probable de la lista.
Cinco riesgos críticos que atravesará DC
El rechazo de los fans
El público de DC ha soportado más de una década de cancelaciones, reinicios, cambios de directiva y promesas rotas. Algo que ha generado un desgaste emocional profundo. La salida de James Gunn, que unificó las expectativas de una gran parte de la comunidad tras el colapso del Snyderverse, podría ser un problema.
En especial, porque amenaza con quebrar la poca confianza que quedaba. En especial, si la audiencia percibe que la nueva administración solo ofrece corporativismo genérico y falta de visión artística a largo plazo. Ninguna franquicia sobrevive sin una base leal que impulse el entusiasmo inicial.
Inestabilidad en la producción y fuga de talento creativo
La constante volatilidad ejecutiva dentro de DC Studios envía una señal de alarma a los mejores directores, guionistas y actores de la industria de Hollywood. El temor a comprometerse con contratos de varios años para proyectos que podrían ser cancelados podría ser un problema.
En particular, porque los creativos prefieren estudios que garanticen estabilidad y respeten su visión. Por lo que DC corre el riesgo de quedarse únicamente con realizadores dóciles que entreguen productos genéricos. Perdiendo, además, la calidad cinematográfica necesaria para competir en el saturado mercado actual.
El modelo Marvel podría no ser ideal para DC
La llegada de un productor enfocado en el modelo tradicional de Marvel Studios puede revivir al peor enemigo histórico de DC. A saber, la interferencia ejecutiva excesiva. Este enfoque fue precisamente el que destruyó el DCEU original entre 2016 y 2017. Repetir el error de priorizar las exigencias de los inversores por encima de la narrativa debilitará el impacto cultural de sus superhéroes.
Pérdida de identidad frente al agotamiento del género
El cine de superhéroes enfrenta un declive global debido a la saturación y la repetición de fórmulas. Para sobresalir en este contexto, DC necesitaba desesperadamente una identidad única y disruptiva. Que era justamente lo que Gunn prometía con su estilo autoral e historias poco convencionales.
Si bajo el mando de Latcham el estudio se limita a imitar la fórmula clásica de Marvel con diez años de retraso, habrá problemas. Mucho más, llegará a un mercado que ya superó esa etapa. Carecer de un sello distintivo propio condenará a la marca a la irrelevancia comercial y crítica.
Confusión masiva en la audiencia general
Mantener a Gunn y Safran como productores de proyectos ya iniciados, mientras Latcham traza un nuevo rumbo, puede producir confusión. En específico, porque el espectador promedio no sigue las noticias corporativas y le costará entender qué ocurre con exactitud. Mucho más si las películas y proyectos se completan entre sí, son un universo nuevo o premisas conectadas.
Esta confusión fragmenta el mercado, diluye el impacto publicitario de los estrenos y ahuyenta al público casual. Este último, un punto vital para sostener taquillas multimillonarias.

articles.title: Zomato-parent Eternal reworking 2030 EV delivery target amid fleet expansion, EV adoption
articles.text:
Zomato-parent Eternal reworking 2030 EV delivery target amid fleet expansion, EV adoption
The company is working towards a revised timeline, factoring in the availability of electric vehicles, supporting government policies, and the transportation requirements of its various businesses.
While remaining committed to green mobility, Zomato and Blinkit parent Eternal is reassessing its 2030 target for a 100% electric delivery fleet due to rapid business expansion and an evolving EV ecosystem.
In an interview with PTI, Anjalli Ravi Kumar, Chief Sustainability Officer at Eternal, said the company is working towards a revised timeline, factoring in the availability of electric vehicles (EVs), supporting government policies, and the transportation requirements of its various businesses.
"We are still committed to electrifying the fleet. We are deeply committed to it because it still makes economic sense," she said.
However, acknowledging that the earlier deadline may not be achievable, Kumar said the company's operations had expanded considerably since the original target was set.
"It doesn't look feasible because, beyond the penetration numbers, our business is also growing massively. When we set the target, there were only 1.5 lakh monthly active riders on Zomato. Today, there are 12 lakh riders across Zomato and Blinkit," she said.
On whether the company could commit to a revised target, possibly by 2035, Kumar said it was working towards a date, with the pace of EV policy implementation also likely to influence the decision.
"We are actively working towards a date. Some of it will depend on the government as well, in terms of whether EV policies have rolled out across the country sufficiently for us to commit to 2035. We are very hopeful. But bear in mind that we have other businesses as well.
“For instance, Hyperpure also uses a lot of delivery vehicles, and those are four-wheeler deliveries involving trucks and smaller commercial vehicles. So, the new EV target for the Eternal Group needs to factor in all kinds of transportation, not just the two-wheeler segment. We can't think about individual businesses anymore. When we set a target, we have to set it for the group. That's our thinking," she said.
Despite the challenges, the company said its delivery fleet was already seeing higher EV adoption than the broader Indian two-wheeler market. Kumar said the company's approach was to encourage partners to adopt EVs through financial incentives, greater access to rental options and awareness initiatives, rather than mandate a particular vehicle choice.
"In our previous estimation, which was done around last December, EV penetration in the market was only around 6-7%. Within our own fleet, there were already about 12-13% of partners using EVs. So, we were already at almost double the market penetration," she said.
One measure encouraging EV adoption is Zomato's equal-benefit policy, under which delivery partners using EVs are paid as much as those using petrol-powered vehicles, despite the lower operating costs.
Kumar said the company also facilitates access to EVs through rental options on its delivery partner app and initiatives such as the EV Bazaar, which familiarises partners with different models available in the market.
At the same time, she said, the scale of its delivery operations makes access and affordability important considerations, particularly as the company onboards large numbers of partners across cities.
"To maintain a base of 12 lakh riders a month, I need to onboard 30 lakh people a year. Now, the question is whether 30 lakh people across 900 cities will all be able to access an EV reliably.
“That's an important question, and this is just the number for this year. Tomorrow, it could be 35 lakh, right? Can I guarantee that all 30 lakh people joining us will have access to an EV across 900 cities? I'm not in a position to make that guarantee, and I don't know when I will," she said.
Kumar also stressed the importance of designing EV policies that account for the livelihoods and financial circumstances of delivery partners, who generally arrange their own vehicles.
She added that the company was advocating worker-friendly EV policies to ensure that the transition to cleaner mobility did not restrict employment opportunities for people who may not be in a position to purchase EVs.
Beyond electric mobility, Eternal is also working with restaurant partners to encourage the adoption of sustainable packaging through initiatives such as PackSwitch, an interactive website that helps restaurants identify alternatives to plastic packaging based on the dishes they serve.
Kumar said the company was working to address three key barriers to the adoption of sustainable packaging—complexity, convenience and cost—by helping restaurants discover suitable alternatives, improve access to suppliers and connect with startups developing new solutions.
Through its Hyperpure business, the company sold more than 3,000 metric tonnes of sustainable packaging to 50,000 restaurants last year.
On the consumer front, more than 10,000 restaurants across over 400 cities have received Zomato's low-plastic packaging tag after the company verified that the packaging used for their main menu was sustainable in nature.

articles.title: Elizabeth Wakefield, asesora financiera: “Tener todo el dinero en una cuenta corriente es uno de los principales errores que mucha gente comete”
articles.text:
Una buena forma de empezar a controlar tus finanzas es separar tus fondos en diferentes cuentas. Por ejemplo, no conviene poner todos tus ahorros en la cuenta en la que tengas los fondos con los que pago los recibos. Y es que esto es algo que viene bien hacerlo desde el principio. Elizabeth Wakefield es una asesora financiera que ha participado en el pódcast “Tiene sentido”, donde ha recomendado esta separación.
Por ello, es importante diferenciar el dinero que tenemos en nuestra cuenta corriente, ese que usamos para realizar nuestras operaciones diarias, de nuestro colchón de seguridad.
Por ejemplo, es muy parecido a cómo organizamos nuestra casa. Los calcetines no se pueden mezclar con los tenedores ni con ninguna herramienta. Cada cuenta debe cumplir un objetivo. De esta forma sabremos cuánto debemos destinar a cada necesidad antes de usarlo.
Separar los recibos, las emergencias y las vacaciones
La primera cuenta es la principal. Aquí son los ingresos los que entran y los pagos habituales los que salen. Es decir, aquí es donde gastamos nuestro dinero.
En este caso es recomendable abrir una nueva cuenta (preferentemente con intereses) que será nuestro colchón de seguridad. Es decir, es el dinero que vamos a usar en caso de urgencia. Por tanto, no es conveniente que sirva para pagar las compras habituales del mes.
Además de estos gastos, tenemos otros que sabemos que van a llegar. Wakefield llama periodificaciones a la planificación de estos gastos. También podemos ahorrar en una cuenta específica para estos gastos. Por ejemplo, supongamos que tenemos que viajar y queremos irnos de vacaciones. Tenemos que ahorrar 2.500 euros. En lugar de esperar hasta el momento de viajar, podemos empezar a ahorrar en los meses previos. Para ello podemos automatizar las transferencias.
Sería bueno ahorrar 150 euros/mes (o 200 euros/mes). Esto es solo un ejemplo. No hay ningún plazo determinado para alcanzar los 2.500 euros. Es decir, vamos a ir guardándolo antes de que llegue el momento de pagar.
También es importante analizar los gastos periódicos que tenemos. Por ejemplo, existen muchas cuotas y suscripciones que mantenemos por inercia. Por ello es relevante analizar qué servicios seguimos pagando pero que ya no utilizamos. Además, hay que pensar si el gasto que vamos a realizar es compatible con nuestro presupuesto. Es decir, antes de comprar debemos pensar si es algo que podemos permitirnos.
Si es financiado, debemos tener en cuenta el verdadero coste. Es importante conocer la diferencia entre el TIN (tipo de interés nominal) y la TAE (tasa anual equivalente). El primero es el precio de prestar el dinero (según explica el Banco de España). Sin embargo, la TAE es la tasa que incluye, además del TIN, los gastos y comisiones asociados. Es decir, se mide en términos de porcentaje anual. De esta forma se puede comparar la financiación.

articles.title: Dev hacks Coway air purifier to cut it off from the cloud, now runs locally in Home Assistant — fan downloads the certificate over plain HTTP, letting a home server stand in for Coway’s
articles.text:
Dev hacks Coway air purifier to cut it off from the cloud, now runs locally in Home Assistant — fan downloads the certificate over plain HTTP, letting a home server stand in for Coway’s
Claude refused to help, ChatGPT obliged, and Coway’s app is no longer in control.
A developer discovered a clever way to cut his Coway Airmega IconS air purifier off from the cloud with the help of a root certificate, allowing local control. The method took advantage of a security hole — the fan downloads the certificate over plain HTTP — and now his Home Assistant server stands in for Coway’s cloud. The result: no more dealing with the unreliable integration that ran through Coway’s IoCare cloud, which broke “at least once or twice a year.”
The developer, Scott J. Goldman, detailed why and how he did it, starting with replacing a dumb Airmega that was “an overpriced box fan with a HEPA filter and an air quality sensor.” The replacement Airmega IconS, which is now discontinued but has Wi-Fi support, had inconsistent Home Assistant (HA) integration. He decided to take matters into his own hands with AI, although he noted that Claude’s guardrails blocked his request to set up his Raspberry Pi to intercept the fan’s traffic under the cybersecurity category, “not even for… uhh… testing purposes.” ChatGPT obliged and wrote the firewall rules, and an AI he doesn’t name later rebuilt the fan’s Bluetooth setup in about 20 minutes.
The fan’s inconsistency had a reason: the IconS has no official HA support, so the route around that relied on a community integration that logs into Coway’s IoCare+ cloud. Coway originally banned the integration for overloading its servers before allowing it after a community dispute. Coway also rebranded its app and cloud from IoCare to IoCare+, which forced a rewrite. Even small HTML layout changes on the pages the integration scraped could break it. On top of that, the company’s servers went offline here and there.
Worse, the developer’s account was banned for running an old integration version, and he lacked remote control for weeks. Originally, all he wanted was for Apple Home’s Good Night scene to switch the purifier on. A common complaint about Internet of Things (IoT) devices like this is that you’re at the mercy of the manufacturer, and support can later evaporate. AI has helped some users like this take back control.
His method involved using the purifier’s security lapse against itself. At setup, it fetches the certificate it trusts over plain, unencrypted HTTP, which can be intercepted and replaced using mitmproxy/mitmweb with nftables port redirection. The request he saw was a plain HTTP GET for AmazonRootCA1.pem from an S3 bucket in AWS’s Seoul region. He then had his proxy serve its own CA to the fan, and the fan made HTTPS requests to Coway’s cert server, which included downloads of a device certificate and private key. Another proxy plugin then swapped his own key into that response.
The fan’s commands ran over MQTT, a lightweight messaging protocol common in smart-home devices, secured with TLS on port 8883 and routed through AWS IoT. The proxy doesn’t decode MQTT, but it showed the raw stream, which the unnamed AI mapped to his app button presses.
He had first considered exploiting eMudhra, a certificate authority whose private keys turned out to be trivially weak last month, which would have involved forging a certificate. That wasn’t necessary because of the plain-HTTP download. Self-signed certificates are nothing new to enthusiasts; this just took a little extra work and avoided the eMudhra plan’s reliance on several things lining up.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Doing the Bluetooth work by hand would have taken hours or even days, he estimated. The unnamed AI also drove an Android phone over adb to read its Bluetooth logs and reconstruct the protocol.
The project is offered as coway-local, which allows the fan to be connected to HA directly, and from there to Apple Home. A Web Bluetooth page, openable in Chrome on a Mac or Android device near the fan, sends the Wi-Fi details. That Bluetooth setup also carries the fan’s certificate URLs, so coway-local points them at the HA server and no traffic interception is needed. The Wi-Fi password goes to the fan over Bluetooth; HA never stores it, and the setup link expires after 15 minutes. The integration runs its own MQTT broker, so the fan now talks to HA instead of AWS.
HA Core 2026.10.2 or newer is needed with a fixed LAN address and 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi. There’s a catch: using it disconnects the fan from Coway’s cloud, so Coway’s app is no longer able to control it. It’s also experimental and tested only on the IconS (AP-1022K), and other Coway models may get through Bluetooth setup without actually working.
The features list is incomplete: PM10 and other air-quality metrics, filter alerts, and firmware updates aren’t implemented yet. He suspects Coway’s cloud could eventually be discontinued or come with a service fee, and a local path is insurance against that. At least for him, this brings satisfaction, as “Now, I can finally click Good Night.”

articles.title: How 007 First Light composers gave the game’s soundtrack ‘a gentle nudge into the modern day’ — ‘One of the great things about this franchise is its ability to stay current and adapt’
articles.text:
007 First Light composers reveal their inspirations for the game’s soundtrack — ‘Our mission we set ourselves was to give the franchise a gentle nudge into the modern day, without completely reinventing it’
"One of the great things about this franchise is its ability to stay current and adapt"
- 007 First Light composers Joe Henson and Alexis Smith share how they tried to nudge the Bond franchise into "the modern day"
- The composers say they didn't want to "reinvent" Bond and had a "huge" catalogue for inspiration
- They also rewatched the film series "to study the scores in a different light, now that we knew we’d be working on our own"
007 First Light composers Joe Henson and Alexis Smith have explained how they tried to modernize the Bond franchise while retaining its classic roots.
In an interview with TechRadar Gaming, Henson and Smith discussed their inspirations for the game's soundtrack and revealed that their primary goal was to push the franchise into a more contemporary direction while keeping the familiar elements fans love.
"Luckily there is a huge catalogue of music, film and novels to dive into, and we took inspiration from all of them, as well as other sources not in the Bond world," Henson said. "Our mission we set ourselves was to give the franchise a gentle nudge into the modern day, without completely reinventing it. It was always going to sound like James Bond."
Smith added that he loves the original Ian Fleming novels and used First Light "as an excuse to re-read them on the train into work each day."
"But like we said before, one of the great things about this franchise is its ability to stay current and adapt," he said. "So, the possibility of going some different places with the music was always there."
While the pair's catalogue of inspiration was "huge" and offered plenty of references, Henson confessed that they tried not to look too much at the previous Bond games, but "we took the time to watch the film series to study the scores in a different light, now that we knew we’d be working on our own."
"So many great composers have added their voice to the franchise, from John Barry to Eric Serra, Michael Kamen to Hans Zimmer, and it is fascinating to hear how each one approaches the material," the composer said.

Smith added, "That made it easier, actually. The fact that the music has gone in so many different directions already made us more confident to pursue our own."

articles.title: Why companies still send contracts as email attachments - Tech Guide
articles.text:
A quote is approved within the CRM system. The client agrees, the price is set, and yet, a peculiar ritual often begins: someone downloads a Word file, fills in the details, and emails a PDF.
The recipient prints it out, signs it, and sends back a scan. Or worse, they return a modified version, with no clear indication of what exactly has been changed. Meanwhile, the software remains completely unaware of these developments.
The problem isn’t the PDF itself
Sending a PDF is not, in itself, a bad practice. The format is widely supported and well-suited for sharing documents with a fixed layout. The issues arise primarily around the file. Who has the latest version? Is the recipient authorized to sign? And how does the finance or administration department know that the agreement has been finalized?
An e-signature platform can handle part of this workload. Through a feature like ‘request a signature,’ the client receives a request to sign the contract digitally, allowing the sender to track its status. However, simply replacing an email attachment with a link does not constitute a fully automated process.
A CRM system is not a document archive
Consider a supplier that enters into dozens of maintenance contracts every month. The terms are stored in the CRM, invoicing is handled via accounting software, and the documents end up in a shared folder. If the contract duration changes, someone must verify that all three systems still contain the same information, a process that is prone to error.
Effective document generation, therefore, begins with the source data. For instance, a template can automatically pull the client’s name, the contract duration, and the agreed-upon price directly from the CRM. The application generates a document from this data and records the specific information used to create it. This is important: if a price is adjusted later, the signed contract should not automatically change as a result.
Webhooks are useful, but not infallible
Integration with an e-signature platform typically takes place via an API. The business software sends the document and receives an identification number in return, which can then be used to check the document’s status. Many services also offer webhooks notifications sent to a pre-configured address whenever someone opens, declines, or signs a document.
Such a notification does not guarantee that the receiving application will process it exactly once. In the event of a time-out, a platform might resend the same event. Developers must therefore verify whether an event has already been processed, for instance by checking a unique event ID. Furthermore, the recipient must verify that the webhook actually originated from the platform; otherwise, a forged request could incorrectly mark a contract as ‘signed.’
An image of a signature proves little
A scribble made with a mouse may look familiar, but on its own, it says very little about the signer’s identity. The same applies to a scanned signature at the bottom of a PDF. Its legal and technical value depends on the entire signing process, including how the signer is identified and how the integrity of the document is maintained.
The archive is part of the workflow
The process does not end with the signature. The final version must be stored in the appropriate location, ideally accompanied by relevant data regarding the signing process. A filename like “contract_new_final3.pdf” is of little help here. A unique contract number, along with metadata concerning the client, date, and duration, makes documents far easier to retrieve. It must also be clear who has access to these documents; for instance, a signed employment contract should not be accessible to every employee who happens to have access to the shared storage system.
The retention period also warrants attention. Not every document may, or should be, stored for the same length of time. An automated archive lacking a deletion policy will eventually become a collection of outdated personal data and agreements that no one ever looks at again. Backups further complicate this, as a deleted document may persist within them for some time. Consequently, the most challenging aspect of document automation is not the act of signing itself, but rather determining how the data is handled both before and after that moment.

articles.title: Nvidia se está planteando una decisión radical para dejar de depender de Samsung en la producción de memoria
articles.text:
La escasez de memoria provocada por el auge de la IA es ya uno de los mayores problemas de suministro del sector tecnológico. Los precios se han disparado y los fabricantes prevén que se prolongue hasta, al menos, 2028. Nvidia, que es una de las que ha impulsado esa crisis, se ha cansado de depender de que sólo unas pocas fabriquen la memoria para sus tarjetas.
Así que se ha planteado producir su propia memoria avanzada, al menos según una filtración.
En corto. Todo viene de un artículo publicado por The Information en el que se adelantó que TSMC había empezado a trazar los planes para fabricar 3D RAM a petición de Nvidia. TSMC tiene su propia hoja de ruta, pero Nvidia es el 'cliente A' de la empresa taiwanesa y, en la situación actual, es evidente que tiene mano para realizar este tipo de peticiones.
El medio citaba dos fuentes con conocimiento directo del asunto y Reuters recogió la información, aunque no pudo confirmarla de forma independiente. Según el informe inicial, TSMC podría comprar una fábrica y reconvertirla en una planta para producir memoria en un movimiento similar al que ya han hecho compañías como Micron (esta sí, especializada en memoria).
El informe también señalaba que el proyecto sería liderado por Hsu Kuo-chin, vicepresidente que supervisa el empaquetado avanzado en TSMC y que ya fue directivo de Micron al frente de sus operaciones en Taiwán.
La esquiva de TSMC. La historia tiene un giro porque, un día después, un portavoz de TSMC comentó a Tom's Hardware que la empresa está centrada en su negocio de fundición de circuitos integrados y que pretende seguir siendo una fundición de chips lógicos. No es una negativa explícita del plan.
Sin embargo, esto de la memoria no sería del todo nuevo para TSMC. En pocas palabras, la DRAM es la memoria que almacena datos de forma temporal durante el funcionamiento del dispositivo. La convencional tiene sus celdas en una capa horizontal, pero la 3D RAM las apila en varios niveles para aumentar la capacidad sin ampliar la superficie. No es lo mismo que la HBM que usan las GPU de IA porque esa apila chips de memoria completos, no las celdas.
Tiene sentido. TSMC ya participa en cierto modo en la cadena de la HBM y en 2024 se alió con la surcoreana SK Hynix para desarrollar la capa lógica que serviría como base de futuros chips HBM. Además, la petición llega justo después de otra demanda de Nvidia hace apenas unas semanas. Como apuntó el medio surcoreano Seoul Economic Daily, Nvidia habría pedido a Samsung, SK Hynix y Micron que usaran el proceso de 3 nanómetros de TSMC para la capa base de NVHBM.
Se trata de la HBM personalizada por la compañía para cumplir sus requisitos y Samsung, tras una revisión interna, habría aceptado, moviendo la producción de la capa base de NVHBM a TSMC, pero manteniendo su producción propia para la HBM estándar para otros clientes. Y Nvidia, claro, quiere que todo vaya para ella, por lo que el siguiente paso es "fabricarla" ella misma. Y quién mejor que una TSMC con la que mantiene una relación tan estrecha.
Suministro roto. Pero bueno, aunque lo publicado por The Information fuera una filtración y TSMC haya esquivado el asunto, es evidente que el suministro de memoria es un problema. Estoy dejando a un lado la crisis para consumidores porque esto ya es algo que hemos tocado largo y tendido, pero centrándome en las grandes de la IA y su aparente objetivo de crecimiento infinito, necesitan memoria y tanto las surcoreanas como la estadounidense Micron no dan abasto.
Aunque todas se están moviendo para ampliar instalaciones, la creación de las salas limpias y los procesos para aumentar la fabricación de DRAM son largos y complejos. Y no es tan sencillo como simplemente poner más máquinas a funcionar porque estamos en un punto en el que todo lo que se tenía que vender para los próximos años ya se ha vendido. La demanda es bestial y la industria de la IA se ha topado con el lastre de que sólo tres compañías sean las que manejan el negocio.
Veremos qué ocurre con Nvidia y si finalmente pasa a tener suministradores exclusivos de su memoria porque estamos en las puertas de la era agéntica y eso necesita más memoria.

articles.title: Dans l’affaire NVIDIA Singapour dit manquer de preuves pour poursuivre Alice Huang
articles.text:
Singapour n’a jamais enquêté sur les liens d’Alice Huang avec la Chine, assure son ministère de l’Intérieur, en réponse à un article du Wall Street Journal. La police de la cité-État poursuit en revanche ses investigations sur Megaspeed, l’entreprise de centres de données qu’Alice Huang a dirigée.
Dans les épisodes précédents de l'affaire NVIDIA, le New York Times avait révélé que le renseignement américain soupçonnait Alice Huang de recueillir des informations sur Jensen Huang pour le compte de Pékin. Le patron de NVIDIA a ensuite reconnu une liaison, sans citer le nom de sa maîtresse, avant de quitter la direction de l’entreprise qu’il avait cofondée en 1993. Le lendemain des révélations du New York Times, le Wall Street Journal affirmait que les autorités de Singapour, siège de Megaspeed, s’inquiétaient elles aussi de cette relation. Le ministère de l’Intérieur singapourien a démenti ces informations point par point, et il a rendu publics ses échanges avec le journal.
Le ministère publie ses échanges avec le Wall Street Journal
D’après le quotidien américain, des responsables singapouriens s’inquiétaient de la proximité d’Alice Huang avec Jensen Huang, ou la soupçonnaient de renseigner les services chinois. Ils auraient aussi enquêté à part sur ses liens avec la Chine. « Ni le gouvernement de Singapour ni ses responsables n’ont tenu ces propos, et aucune enquête de ce type n’a été menée au sujet d’Alice Huang », souligne le ministère dans sa mise au point.
Pour étayer sa réponse, le ministère a publié la question envoyée par le journal avant la parution de l’article. Le Wall Street Journal demandait si le service de renseignement de Singapour soupçonnait Alice Huang de travailler pour le ministère chinois de la Sécurité d’État, le principal service d’espionnage de Pékin. Le quotidien affirmait aussi que les autorités l’avaient interrogée en 2025, puis relâchée.
Dans leur réponse, transmise avant la parution de l’article, les autorités ne parlent pas d’Alice Huang. Elles évoquent seulement Megaspeed. Et dans sa mise au point, le ministère ne dit rien de l’interrogatoire de 2025.
Singapour n’applique pas les restrictions américaines sur les puces
La police de Singapour enquête toujours sur Megaspeed, que Washington soupçonne d’avoir aidé des entreprises chinoises à se procurer des puces NVIDIA interdites d’exportation vers la Chine. Selon The Information, le réseau d’entreprises monté par Alice Huang, son mari et sa sœur entre la Chine et Singapour aurait permis de livrer près de 240 000 puces NVIDIA à des sociétés chinoises, pour au moins 7,5 milliards de dollars. Comme l’expliquent les autorités singapouriennes dans leur réponse au journal, « l’enquête sur Megaspeed est toujours en cours, et nous ne pouvons pas faire d’autres commentaires à ce stade ».
Le gouvernement rappelle surtout que Singapour n’applique pas les restrictions à l’exportation imposées unilatéralement par d’autres pays. Il interdit en revanche aux entreprises de se servir de leur implantation à Singapour pour contourner ces règles étrangères, et il poursuit la fraude. Depuis février 2025, Singapour a ainsi inculpé quatre personnes et quatre sociétés pour avoir trompé des fournisseurs de serveurs, avec des chefs d’accusation passibles chacun de 20 ans de prison.
Megaspeed, de son côté, dément tout transfert illégal de puces vers la Chine.

articles.title: Arbeitstrend Microshifting: So soll er die Produktivität steigern und Stress reduzieren
articles.text:
Statt 9-to-5: Warum immer mehr Beschäftigte im Homeoffice auf „Microshifting“ setzen
Die Arbeitswelt bringt immer wieder neue Trends hervor, die den Arbeitsalltag von Angestellten bestimmen. Selbst außerhalb des Büros, im Homeoffice, gibt es Trends wie den Soft Off Day, um dem immer anwachsenden Arbeitspensum und Druck zu entgehen. Der Trend Microshifting schlägt in eine ähnliche Kerbe, lässt aber die Produktivität nicht auf der Strecke.
Was ist Microshifting?
Bei Microshifting geht es darum, den Arbeitstag nicht als 9-to-5-Block zu sehen, sondern ihn in kleinere Blöcke aufzuteilen. Nicht jeder der Blöcke muss dabei zwangsläufig mit Arbeit gefüllt sein. Dank des flexiblen Homeoffice können Arbeitende etwa um 8 Uhr ihren Arbeitstag beginnen und die wichtigsten Aufgaben erledigen, bevor sie dann einen kurzen Block einschieben, um beim Supermarkt um die Ecke Erledigungen zu machen.
Danach wird wieder bis zur Mittagspause gearbeitet. Statt nur schnell etwas zu essen, verlängern Arbeitnehmer:innen dann die Pause etwas und bringen noch eine schnelle Session im Fitnessstudio unter, bevor es für einen weiteren Block wieder an den Arbeitsplatz geht. Zu guter Letzt holen sie noch den Nachwuchs aus der Kita und loggen sich ein letztes Mal von Zuhause ein, um den nächsten Arbeitstag vorzubereiten.
Obwohl im Laufe des Tages auch viele Aufgaben im Haushalt und des persönlichen Lebens erledigt wurden, kommt die Arbeit nicht zu kurz. Microshifter:innen behalten den Überblick über alle anliegenden Aufgaben und erfüllen sie fristgerecht. Arbeitsalltag und Privatleben verschmelzen im Grunde miteinander. Nicht jeder Tag ist dabei gleich. Ohne große Ankündigung oder Planung können die Abläufe immer wieder angepasst werden.
Welche Vor- und Nachteile hat Microshifting?
Da der Trend schon seit Ende 2025 existiert und seither mehrere Anhänger:innen gefunden hat, gibt es auch schon mehrere Berichte zu den Vor- und Nachteilen des Microshiftings. Ein klarer Vorteil ist, dass sich Arbeitnehmer:innen ihren Tag deutlich freier und flexibler gestalten können. Wer seine Pause im Fitnessstudio verlängert oder schon Wege schnell erledigen kann, kann im Anschluss konzentrierter weiterarbeiten. Zudem reduziert Microshifting laut einer Untersuchung von Owl Labs, Hersteller von Gadgets für Video-Meetings, bei vielen Arbeitnehmer:innen das Gefühl, an den Schreibtisch gebunden zu sein. Das kann die Moral steigern und die Gefahren von zu viel Stress senken.
Microshifting kann aber auch Schattenseiten haben. Wenn Arbeitnehmer:innen im Homeoffice ständig zwischen Arbeit und Privatleben wechseln, verschwimmen die Grenzen. Sie sind nie in einem der beiden Bereiche wirklich präsent. Durch die eingeschobenen Blöcke kann sich zudem der Tag deutlich länger anfühlen und den Stresslevel erhöhen, statt ihn zu senken.
Ebenso besteht die Gefahr, dass die Arbeit unter den Blöcken leidet. Microshifting kann zwar die Produktivität einzelner steigern, aber einem größeren Team schaden. Wenn mehrere Arbeitnehmer:innen dem Trend nachgehen, können sie womöglich nie richtig zusammenarbeiten. Die Kommunikation und die Agilität innerhalb des Unternehmens bleiben mittelfristig auf der Strecke.
Wie können Arbeitgeber:innen mit Microshifting umgehen?
Viele Arbeitgeber:innen dürften Microshifting deshalb kritischer gegenüberstehen. Führungskräfte könnten das Vertrauen in Angestellte verlieren, die immer wieder vom Arbeitsplatz im Homeoffice verschwinden, um private Angelegenheiten zu erledigen. Um Microshifting kontrollierter betreiben zu können, gibt Owl Labs Unternehmen zwei Empfehlungen. So können sie die Vorzüge des Arbeitstrends bieten und die Nachteile womöglich reduzieren.
Zunächst sollten feste Kollaborationsstunden festgelegt werden. In einem Zeitraum von vier bis fünf Stunden müssen alle Mitarbeiter:innen abrufbar sein – sei es für Meetings oder schnelle Absprachen. Außerhalb dieses Blocks können Arbeitnehmer:innen ihre Zeit freier einteilen, solange die Arbeit nicht auf der Strecke bleibt. Das ist auch die Quintessenz des zweiten Tipps.
Laut Owl Labs sollten Arbeitgeber:innen nicht die Arbeitszeiten, sondern den Output ihrer Angestellten messen. Wenn Arbeitnehmer:innen ihre Ziele durchweg erreichen, Projekte rechtzeitig abschließen und zu den wichtigsten Zeiten erreichbar sind, sollten sie die Freiheit haben, ihre privaten Termine mit der Arbeit zu vereinen.

articles.title: 5 lessons from book Be Delusional by Harinder Singh Pelia
articles.text:
5 lessons from book Be Delusional by Harinder Singh Pelia
Discover five powerful lessons from Be Delusional by Harinder Singh Pelia on self-belief, ambition, confidence and turning big dreams into reality.
What if believing in yourself before the world does is the first step towards achieving something extraordinary?
Most people wait for evidence before they start believing in their potential. They look for approval, reassurance and the right circumstances before pursuing ambitious goals. But what if the secret to success lies in believing that you are capable long before you have proof?
In Be Delusional: Bend Reality to Your Beliefs, author Harinder Singh Pelia explores how strong self-belief can influence ambition, behaviour and achievement. Drawing on psychology, real-life stories and practical exercises, the book challenges readers to question their limitations and develop the confidence to pursue seemingly impossible goals.
The book draws examples from personalities such as Sylvester Stallone, Lady Gaga and Kanye West, who believed in their abilities even when circumstances did not support their ambitions.
Here are five lessons to learn from Be Delusional that can change the way you approach your goals and ambitions.
5 lessons from Be Delusional by Harinder Singh Pelia
1. Believe in yourself before you have proof
One of the central ideas of the book is that successful people often believe in their abilities before they have anything to show for them. They do not necessarily wait for recognition, achievements or approval to develop confidence in themselves.
Consider Sylvester Stallone, who believed strongly in his potential as an actor despite facing rejection. Similarly, Lady Gaga continued pursuing her musical ambitions despite setbacks.
Their stories highlight an important lesson: confidence does not always come after success. Sometimes, it is what motivates people to work towards success in the first place.
The takeaway: Stop waiting for external validation to believe in your potential. Give yourself permission to pursue ambitions even when the results are uncertain.
2. Change the story you tell yourself
The way we describe ourselves can influence how we approach opportunities and challenges. If you constantly tell yourself that you are not talented enough, not experienced enough or not capable of achieving something, you may eventually start behaving as though those beliefs are facts.
Drawing on psychologist Dan McAdams' Narrative Identity Theory, Pelia explores how the stories people tell themselves contribute to their sense of identity.
Changing your internal narrative does not mean ignoring your weaknesses. It means refusing to let your past experiences become permanent definitions of who you are.
The takeaway: Instead of repeatedly telling yourself why you cannot achieve something, start building a narrative around the person you want to become.
3. Act like the person you want to become
Believing in a future version of yourself is important, but belief becomes meaningful when it influences your behaviour.
The book introduces a concept called the 'Lie Ladder', which describes different levels of belief and the behaviours associated with them. At the third level, a person begins acting like their desired future self in specific situations rather than simply thinking about their ambitions.
For instance, someone who wants to become a successful entrepreneur can start making decisions, building skills and taking responsibilities that align with that identity.
You do not have to wait until you achieve your goal to begin developing the habits associated with it.
The takeaway: Do not just visualise your future self. Start behaving like that person through small, consistent actions.
4. Stop letting other people's doubts define you
Ambitious goals often invite criticism, especially when they seem unrealistic to others. Friends, colleagues and even family members may question your decisions because they cannot see the possibilities you imagine.
However, other people's opinions do not necessarily determine what you are capable of achieving.
The stories explored in Be Delusional demonstrate how some successful personalities continued believing in their abilities despite rejection and scepticism. Their conviction helped them persist when external circumstances offered little encouragement.
This does not mean ignoring constructive criticism. Instead, it means learning to distinguish between useful feedback and opinions that simply discourage you.
The takeaway: Listen to advice that helps you grow, but do not allow someone else's limited expectations to become your own.
5. Turn ambitious beliefs into action
There is a difference between imagining an extraordinary future and actively working towards it. Positive thinking alone cannot guarantee success. It needs to be supported by effort, preparation, commitment and the willingness to take risks.
Pelia's book makes this distinction through its combination of psychological insights, real-world examples and practical exercises. It encourages readers to move beyond passive dreaming and develop a stronger commitment to their ambitions.
Whether you want to build a business, pursue a creative career or achieve a personal milestone, your beliefs should influence the decisions you make today.
The takeaway: Let your ambitions shape your actions. Believe in possibilities, but put in the work required to make them real.
Final thoughts
Be Delusional: Bend Reality to Your Beliefs by Harinder Singh Pelia challenges the conventional idea that people need evidence of success before they can believe in themselves.
The book presents self-belief as something that can be developed through the stories we tell ourselves, the identities we build and the actions we take. Its central message is not about blindly ignoring reality but about refusing to let current circumstances dictate the limits of future possibilities.
Sometimes, the first person who needs to believe in your dreams is you. And perhaps, being a little unreasonable about what you can achieve is exactly what encourages you to take the first step.

articles.title: Un avion que vous n’entendez pas peut révéler où vous avez tourné une vidéo
articles.text:
Le 2 novembre, le vidéaste Colsto, spécialiste de la géolocalisation à partir d’indices publics, a publié une démonstration de 29 minutes intitulée I discovered a sound that leaks your exact location. À partir des images d’une simple caméra de surveillance (des arbres, une rivière et rien d’autre), il affirme avoir retrouvé l’endroit du tournage à une centaine de mètres près, en ne connaissant que le jour de l’enregistrement et le pays. Son seul indice : deux avions à hélice passés hors de portée de l’oreille, dont la trace subsiste dans les basses fréquences de la bande-son.
Comment un avion que vous n’entendez pas peut-il vous trahir ?
Tout part de l’effet Doppler, celui qui fait baisser la sirène d’une ambulance une fois qu’elle vous a dépassé. Un moteur d’avion produit le même glissement de fréquence, y compris à plusieurs kilomètres de distance. Les sons graves portent loin, et un micro de téléphone ou de caméra les capte là où votre oreille ne perçoit rien. Sur un spectrogramme, la représentation visuelle des fréquences d’un enregistrement, chaque survol dessine une courbe en S dont la forme livre la vitesse de l’appareil, sa distance minimale et l’instant exact de son passage.
L’autre moitié de l’équation vient des avions eux-mêmes : presque tous diffusent en continu leur position, leur altitude et leur vitesse via le protocole ADS-B, que des réseaux d’amateurs archivent jour après jour. Dans sa démonstration, le vidéaste repère deux survols espacés de 920 secondes, en déduit environ 70 000 lieux candidats, puis élimine tous ceux où un troisième appareil aurait dû s’entendre dans l’intervalle. Pour les quelque 15 000 points restants, il simule la courbe que chaque position aurait enregistrée et la compare à la vraie. Un seul endroit colle, et Street View y montre le même alignement d’arbres qu’à l’image, poteau de la caméra compris.
L’audio d’origine et le code n’ont pas été publiés : la précision d’une centaine de mètres reste donc une affirmation de l’auteur, que personne n’a pu refaire à l’identique. Le principe, lui, s’appuie sur un précédent bien établi, la criminalistique datant depuis des années des enregistrements en comparant le ronflement du réseau électrique capté par le micro aux archives des opérateurs. Ici, le même raisonnement s’applique à l’espace, avec les archives de vol en guise de registre.
L’IA a reconstruit l’outil en deux jours, et pourrait s’y faire piéger
Colsto n’a diffusé ni code ni logiciel, précaution qui n’aura tenu que quelques heures. Moins de deux jours après la vidéo, au moins huit dépôts open source reproduisant la méthode étaient en ligne, certains assemblés par des agents de programmation. L’une de ces répliques retrouve l’enregistrement qu’il a publié en défi à 86 mètres près, en balayant l’ensemble du territoire américain. Il lui faut pour cela deux survols et l’heure de début à deux minutes près. Avec un seul avion ou un horaire incertain, en revanche, ces mêmes outils échouent ou renoncent à conclure, et les webcams publiques qu’ils ont testées à l’aveugle n’ont jamais été localisées.
Le 3 novembre, Adam Holter, qui documente l’IA sur X, a fait vérifier par Codex, l’agent de programmation d’OpenAI, 120 vidéos générées par intelligence artificielle. Aucune ne contiendrait de courbe Doppler d’avion dans les basses fréquences, et le grave produit par les modèles serait « totalement différent » de celui d’un vrai enregistrement. Le critère ne fonctionne toutefois que dans un sens, l’intéressé le reconnaît lui-même, puisque la plupart des vraies vidéos n’en contiennent pas davantage. Une courbe cohérente avec un vol réellement archivé ce jour-là vaudrait en revanche certificat d’authenticité, du moins jusqu’à ce que les générateurs apprennent à l’imiter, objection opposée dès la publication du fil.
 After having Codex check 120 different generated videos, models do NOT generate low-frequency airplane Dopplers https://t.co/RTB0eRHdlX
— Adam Holter (@AdamHoltererer) November 3, 2026
En Europe, la diffusion ADS-B n’est obligatoire que depuis le 7 décembre 2020, et seulement pour les appareils de plus de 5,7 tonnes ou dépassant les 250 nœuds. Les petits avions à hélice, précisément les plus lisibles sur un spectrogramme, échappent donc pour la plupart à l’obligation, quand la règle américaine couvre depuis janvier 2020 l’essentiel des espaces aériens surveillés. Toutes les localisations réussies publiées à ce jour concernent d’ailleurs des enregistrements américains, et l’archive communautaire qu’exploitent ces répliques ne remonte qu’à 2023.

articles.title: The Hidden Costs of Patchwork Business Tools - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Most businesses don’t notice workflow problems all at once. They show up slowly.
A team spends extra time chasing approvals. Customer information lives in three different places. Reporting takes longer than expected. Employees keep switching between tools just to complete one task. None of these issues seem dramatic on their own, but together they create a system that feels heavier than it should.
That’s the real cost of a patchwork technology stack. It’s not just about licensing fees. It’s about the drag created when software doesn’t work together in a practical, business-friendly way.
Why tool sprawl becomes a business problem
At first, adding new software feels like progress.
One platform helps with communication. Another handles project management. A third improves security. A fourth supports analytics. Before long, the business has assembled a full stack of specialized tools.
The problem is that specialized doesn’t always mean connected. When systems are disconnected, people become the bridge between them. Employees copy information manually, repeat tasks, and lose time moving between platforms. That slows execution, increases mistakes, and makes scaling harder.
For growing companies, this becomes more than a productivity issue. It becomes an operational risk.
Where companies usually look first for solutions
When pressure builds, most businesses respond in predictable ways. They try to cut software costs. They review vendors. They look for security upgrades. They search for small efficiencies that can reduce immediate pressure. That’s why a practical cost-saving move, such as using a Surfshark coupon, can feel like a smart step in the right direction. It helps control one expense while supporting a safer, more reliable digital environment.
But that kind of saving only solves part of the problem.
The larger issue is usually not one overpriced tool. It’s the fact that everyday work is still fragmented across too many systems.
The bigger opportunity is workflow design
The companies that improve fastest usually stop asking, “Which tool should we add next?” Instead, they ask, “How can we make work move more smoothly across the business?”
That shift matters.
Once you focus on workflow design, you start seeing where technology should support the business instead of complicating it. You can spot repeated tasks, disconnected data, delays in communication, and manual handoffs that shouldn’t exist anymore.
This is also where solutions like an AI gateway fit naturally into the conversation. Rather than forcing teams to live inside disconnected tools, businesses can route requests through a single layer built around real operational needs — whether that means directing work to the right system, pulling information from connected sources, or reducing manual follow-up.
What better workflow planning looks like
A more effective approach usually includes a few key principles.
- Start with process pain, not product hype. Don’t begin with the newest software category. Begin with the real problems inside the business. Look at where teams lose time, where requests get delayed, and where employees depend on manual workarounds just to keep things moving.
- Reduce duplication across systems. If the same information is being entered, checked, or updated in multiple places, there’s an opportunity to simplify. The goal is to reduce repeated work and improve accuracy at the same time.
- Use targeted savings wisely. Cost-saving opportunities still matter. Lowering the expense of a security product or remote access tool can be helpful. But those decisions should support a larger operations plan, not replace one.
- Invest where efficiency compounds. The biggest return often comes from improvements that save time every day. That could mean better integrations, better task routing, or smarter automation around recurring work.
Why this matters for growth
It’s hard to scale a business when everyday work depends on patching systems together by hand.
Eventually, complexity catches up. Teams work harder just to maintain the same level of output. Managers spend more time coordinating. Employees feel the weight of process instead of the benefit of technology.
That’s why workflow strategy matters so much.
The right tools shouldn’t just exist in the same stack. They should all drive one shared business outcome.
The bottom line
A cheaper tool isn’t always a better system. Yes, tactical savings matter. But long-term gains usually come from improving how tools, teams, and tasks work together.
When businesses solve that bigger problem, technology starts to feel less like overhead and more like leverage.

articles.title: Entró en vigor: Es obligatorio tener en casa un protocolo de riesgos laborales para el servicio doméstico
articles.text:
Los empleadores de servicio doméstico tienen la obligación de llevar a cabo una evaluación de riesgos y poner en marcha las medidas preventivas que sean necesarias. Hasta el día 14 de noviembre de 2025 disponían de tiempo para ello. A partir de esa fecha deben haber sido llevadas a cabo.
Quienes quedan afectados son los hogares que tienen condición de empleadores. Hay que tener en cuenta las particularidades del domicilio y las actividades que desempeña el trabajador. Es posible caer en confusiones hablando de protocolo en el hogar. Es importante conocer qué riesgos pueden estar asociados a las actividades que se llevan a cabo. Además de esto, tenemos otras obligaciones de carácter laboral (los requisitos salariales, como explicamos en Genbeta).
En el Real Decreto 893/2024 se incluye el desarrollo de la protección de la seguridad y salud en el servicio del hogar familiar tras haberse suprimido su exclusión de la Ley de Prevención de Riesgos Laborales. En él también se incluye la protección frente a la violencia y acoso en este ámbito.
Cómo evaluar los riesgos y dejar constancia de las medidas
Para facilitar su cumplimiento, el INSST ha puesto a disposición de los empleadores una herramienta que pueden utilizar de manera gratuita. Se puede consultar en Prevencion10.es.
Con esta herramienta podemos conseguir un documento que refleje la evaluación de riesgos en nuestro domicilio. También contiene las medidas de prevención que debemos poner en marcha. Además, se incluyen los materiales de información que debemos proporcionar al trabajador. Podemos registrar la fecha de implantación de las distintas medidas y seguir su cumplimiento. Debe ser coherente con las actividades que se hacen en la vivienda.
Una vez generada la evaluación, procedemos al siguiente paso. En caso de que haya situaciones de riesgo, es el propio empleador quien debe tomar las medidas necesarias para erradicar o minimizar el riesgo. También debe controlarlo. Estas acciones deben documentarse de forma escrita y debe informarse al trabajador (con una copia) de ellas. Es preciso indicar la fecha exacta en que se llevan a cabo.
Esta herramienta está pensada para que pueda ser usada sin conocimientos técnicos. Contratar asesoría profesional no es un requisito general. En el caso de que el empleador tenga capacidad para utilizar correctamente esta herramienta, puede asumir directamente la actividad preventiva. Para ello basta con que tenga capacidad suficiente para utilizarla. Para cumplir con estos requisitos es necesario poner en marcha las medidas pertinentes y documentar las acciones que se realicen.
